title.zh: 卷一百九十三 志第一百四十六 兵七
title.raw: 卷一百九十三 志第一百四十六 兵七 Volume 193 Treatises 146: Military 7

sentences.zh: 兵七

translations.literal: Military 7
translations.idiomatic: Military Affairs VII

sentences.zh: 〈（召募之製）〉

translations.literal: (The System of Recruitment)
translations.idiomatic: (Recruitment Regulations)

sentences.zh: 召募之製起於府衛之廢。

translations.literal: The system of recruitment arose from the abolition of the garrison-guard regiments.
translations.idiomatic: Recruitment as an institution began when the fubing garrison system was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 唐末士卒疲於征役，多亡命者，梁祖令諸軍悉黵麵為字，以識軍號，是為長征之兵。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang, soldiers weary of campaigning often deserted; the Founder of Liang ordered all armies to tattoo characters on the face as unit marks—these were the long-campaign troops.
translations.idiomatic: In late Tang, troops exhausted by constant campaigning often fled. The Later Liang founder ordered every army to tattoo unit marks on recruits' faces, creating the standing expeditionary forces.

sentences.zh: 方其募時，先度人材，次閱走躍，試瞻視，然後黵麵，賜以緡錢、衣履而隸諸籍。

translations.literal: At recruitment they first gauged the man's build, then tested running and leaping and his gaze, then tattooed the face, granted cash strings, clothing and boots, and enrolled them on the registers.
translations.idiomatic: At muster they first measured stature, then tested running, leaping, and eyesight; only then were faces tattooed, cash and kit issued, and names entered on the rolls.

sentences.zh: 國初因之，或募土人就所在團立，或取營伍子弟聽從本軍，或募饑民以補本城，或以有罪配隸給役。

translations.literal: At the founding of the dynasty this continued: sometimes recruiting local natives and organizing them on the spot, sometimes taking sons of camp soldiers from their home unit, sometimes recruiting famine victims to fill the home garrison, or assigning convicts to labor service.
translations.idiomatic: Early Song kept these methods: peasants might be recruited and formed locally; sons of serving soldiers could enlist with their parent commands; famine refugees might fill home garrisons; or convicts could be assigned as labor troops.

sentences.zh: 取之雖非一途，而伉健者遷禁衛，短弱者為廂軍，製以隊伍，束以法令。

translations.literal: Although the sources of recruitment were not one, the stalwart were transferred to the Forbidden Guard, the shorter and weaker to the Provincial Corps, formed into squads and bound by statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Recruits came from many channels, but the fit went to the Palace Guards, the less robust to the Provincial Corps, organized in companies and governed by strict regulations.

sentences.zh: 當其無事時，雖不無爵賞衣廩之費，一有征討，則以之力戰鬥，給漕免，而天下獷悍失職之徒，皆為良民之衛矣。

translations.literal: In times without affairs, although there were still expenses for ranks, rewards, and grain stipends, once there was campaigning they used them to fight in battle and supply transport relief, and the fierce and unemployed of the realm all became guards of good people.
translations.idiomatic: Peacetime still brought costs for ranks, rewards, and rations; but in war these men fought and moved supplies, turning the empire's toughest unemployed into protectors of ordinary citizens.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖揀軍中強勇者號兵樣，分送諸道，令如樣招募。

translations.literal: Initially Taizu selected the strongest in the army and called them soldier models, sending them to the circuits to recruit according to the model.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu first picked the army's strongest men as "model soldiers," sent them to each circuit, and ordered recruitment to match those standards.

sentences.zh: 後更為木梃，差以尺寸高下，謂之等長杖，委長吏、都監度人材取之。

translations.literal: Later they changed to wooden staffs, graded by height of dimensions, called equal-length staffs, and entrusted circuit chief officials and camp supervisors to measure stature and take men.
translations.idiomatic: Later wooden staffs graded by height—the "graded-height staffs"—replaced the models, and circuit administrators and camp supervisors measured recruits against them.

sentences.zh: 當部送闕者，軍頭司覆驗，引對便坐，分隸諸軍。

translations.literal: When the circuit delivered them to court, the Army Head Office re-examined them, presented them in audience at the informal seat, and assigned them to the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: Recruits sent to court were re-tested by the Military Appointment Bureau, presented before the emperor at informal audience, and assigned to regiments.

sentences.zh: 真宗祥符中，重定等杖，自五尺八寸至五尺五寸為五等，諸州部送闕下，及等者隸次軍。

translations.literal: In the Xiangfu period of Zhenzong, height staffs were re-fixed from five chi eight cun to five chi five cun as five grades; circuits delivered to court those meeting the grade and assigned them to successive armies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenzong in the Xiangfu period, height standards were reset in five grades from five foot eight to five foot five; prefectures sent qualified men to court and slotted them by grade.

sentences.zh: 仁宗天聖元年，詔京東西、河北、河東、淮南、陝西路募兵，當部送者刺“指揮”二字，家屬給口糧。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiansheng of Renzong, an edict ordered the Jingdong East and West, Hebei, Hedong, Huainan, and Shaanxi circuits to recruit soldiers; those delivered to court were tattooed with the two characters "command," and families were given grain rations.
translations.idiomatic: In Renzong's first Tiansheng year, circuits from Jingdong through Huainan to Shaanxi were ordered to recruit; men sent to court were tattooed "Command," and their families received rations.

sentences.zh: 兵官代還，以所募多寡為賞罰。

translations.literal: When military officials rotated home, rewards and punishments were based on how many they had recruited.
translations.idiomatic: Officers returning from duty were rewarded or penalized according to their recruitment totals.

sentences.zh: 又詔益、利、梓、夔路歲募民充軍士，及數即部送，分隸奉節、川效忠、川忠節。

translations.literal: Also an edict ordered Yi, Li, Zi, and Kui circuits annually to recruit commoners as soldiers; when the quota was met they were delivered to court and assigned to Fengjie, Chuan Xiaozhong, and Chuan Zhongjie armies.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict required Yi, Li, Zi, and Kui to raise troops yearly; once quotas were met, recruits were sent to court and assigned to the Fengjie, Chuan Loyalty, and Chuan Dedication armies.

sentences.zh: 於是遠方健勇失業之民，悉有所歸。

translations.literal: Thereupon the stalwart and unemployed of distant circuits all had a place to go.
translations.idiomatic: Thus fierce, jobless men from remote circuits all gained employment.

sentences.zh: 慶曆七年，諸路募廂軍及五尺七寸已上者，部送闕下，試補禁衛。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qingli, Provincial Corps recruits and those five chi seven cun or taller were delivered to court and tested for assignment to the Forbidden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingli 7, Provincial Corps men and recruits five foot seven or taller were sent to court for testing into the Palace Guards.

sentences.zh: 至和元年，河北、河東、陝西募就糧兵，騎以四百人、步以五百人為一營。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhihe, Hebei, Hedong, and Shaanxi recruited grain-paid troops; cavalry at four hundred men and infantry at five hundred men formed one battalion.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhihe 1, Hebei, Hedong, and Shaanxi raised "grain-paid" troops, with four hundred cavalry or five hundred infantry per battalion.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐二年復定等仗，自上四軍至武肅、忠靖皆五尺已上，差以寸分而視其奉錢：一千者以五尺八寸、七寸、三寸為三等。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiayou height staffs were again fixed: from the Upper Four Armies to Wusu and Zhongjing all were five chi or above, graded by cun and fen and matched to salary—for one thousand cash, three grades at five chi eight cun, seven cun, and three cun.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiayou 2 height standards were revised again: from the Upper Four Armies through Wusu and Zhongjing all required five foot or more, with pay graded by fractions of an inch—for a one-thousand-cash stipend, three grades at five foot eight, five foot seven, and five foot three.

sentences.zh: 奉錢七百者，以五尺七寸、六寸、五寸為三等。

translations.literal: For salary of seven hundred, three grades at five chi seven cun, six cun, and five cun.
translations.idiomatic: For seven hundred cash, three grades at five foot seven, five foot six, and five foot five.

sentences.zh: 奉錢五百者，以五尺六寸、五寸五分為三等。

translations.literal: For salary of five hundred, three grades at five chi six cun and five cun five fen.
translations.idiomatic: For five hundred cash, three grades at five foot six and five foot five and a half.

sentences.zh: 奉錢四百者，以五尺五寸、四寸五分為二等。

translations.literal: For salary of four hundred, two grades at five chi five cun and four cun five fen.
translations.idiomatic: For four hundred cash, two grades at five foot five and five foot four and a half.

sentences.zh: 奉錢三百者，以五尺五寸、四寸五分、四寸、三寸、二寸為六等。

translations.literal: For salary of three hundred, six grades at five chi five cun, four cun five fen, four cun, three cun, and two cun.
translations.idiomatic: For three hundred cash, six grades from five foot five down to five foot two.

sentences.zh: 奉錢二百者，以五尺四寸、三寸五分、三寸、二寸為四等。

translations.literal: For salary of two hundred, four grades at five chi four cun, three cun five fen, three cun, and two cun.
translations.idiomatic: For two hundred cash, four grades from five foot four to five foot two.

sentences.zh: 不給奉錢者，以五尺二寸或下五寸七指、八指為等。

translations.literal: Those without salary were graded at five chi two cun, or below at five cun seven fingers and eight fingers.
translations.idiomatic: Men without stipends were graded at five foot two or below, down to five foot seven or eight tenths of a cun.

sentences.zh: 唯武嚴、禦營喝探以藝精者充，諸司筦庫執技者不設等杖。

translations.literal: Only Wuyan and Imperial Camp scouts were filled by those skilled in arts; clerks and technicians of various offices did not use height staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wuyan and imperial scout units took men chosen for skill; warehouse clerks and technical specialists were exempt from height grading.

sentences.zh: 七年，御史唐介言：“比歲等募禁軍多小弱，不勝鎧甲，請以初創尺寸為定，敢議減縮者，論以違製。”

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Censor Tang Jie said: "In recent years recruitment of Forbidden Guard has mostly been small and weak, unable to bear armor; please take the original dimensions as fixed, and those daring to discuss reduction shall be punished for violating regulations."
translations.idiomatic: In year 7, Censor Tang Jie reported that recent Palace Guard recruits were often too slight for armor and urged locking heights to the original standards, with penalties for anyone who tried to lower them.

sentences.zh: 詔：“禁軍備戰者，宜著此令。

translations.literal: An edict: "Forbidden Guard prepared for war should follow this order."
translations.idiomatic: The court replied that combat-ready Guards should follow this rule.

sentences.zh: 其備役雄武、宣敕六軍、搭材之類，如軍馬敕。”

translations.literal: Those in reserve—Xiongwu, Xuanchi Six Armies, labor detachments, and the like—follow the Horse Army edict.
translations.idiomatic: Reserve units such as Xiongwu, Xuanchi Six Armies, and labor corps would follow separate cavalry regulations.

sentences.zh: 治平二年，募陝西土民、營伍子弟隸禁軍，一營填止八分。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiping, Shaanxi natives and sons of camp soldiers were recruited for the Forbidden Guard, filling only eight-tenths of each battalion.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiping 2, Shaanxi locals and soldiers' sons filled Palace Guard battalions only to eighty percent of quota.

sentences.zh: 又遣使畿縣、南京、曹、濮、單、陳、許、蔡、亳州募民補虎翼、廣勇，人加賜絹、布各一。

translations.literal: Also envoys were sent to the capital counties, Nanjing, Cao, Pu, Dan, Chen, Xu, Cai, Bozhou to recruit commoners to fill Huyi and Guangyong, each man given an extra bolt of silk and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys also recruited around the capital and in Cao, Pu, Dan, Chen, Xu, Cai, and Bo to fill Huyi and Guangyong units, with an extra bolt of silk and cloth per man.

sentences.zh: 治平四年，詔延州募保捷五營，以備更戍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhiping, an edict ordered Yanzhou to recruit five Baojie battalions for rotation garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiping 4, Yanzhou was ordered to raise five Baojie battalions for rotating frontier service.

sentences.zh: 熙寧元年，詔諸州募饑民補廂軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xining, an edict ordered all circuits to recruit famine victims to fill Provincial Corps.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 1, all circuits were told to recruit famine refugees into the Provincial Corps.

sentences.zh: 二年，樞密院言：“國初邊州無警則罷兵，今既講和，而屯兵至多，徒耗金帛。

translations.literal: In the second year, the Bureau of Military Affairs reported: "At the founding, frontier circuits disbanded troops when there was no alarm; now peace has been negotiated but garrison troops are extremely numerous, wasting silk and cash in vain."
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 2, the Bureau of Military Affairs noted that early Song had demobilized frontier troops in peacetime, yet after the peace treaty garrisons had swollen, wasting vast sums.

sentences.zh: 若於近裏糧賤處增募營兵，但令往戍極邊，甚為便計。”

translations.literal: "If in nearby districts where grain is cheap more camp troops are increased, but only sent to garrison the extreme frontier, this would be a very convenient plan."
translations.idiomatic: Raising more troops in cheap-grain districts inland and posting them only on the far frontier would be far more efficient.

sentences.zh: 帝與文彥博及韓絳、陳升之、呂公弼等議之，或以為自古皆募營兵，遇事息即罷，或以為緣邊之兵不可多減。

translations.literal: The Emperor discussed with Wen Yanbo, Han Jiang, Chen Shengzhi, Lü Gongbi, and others; some held that from antiquity camp troops were recruited and disbanded when affairs settled, others that frontier troops could not be much reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted Wen Yanbo, Han Jiang, Chen Shengzhi, and Lü Gongbi; some argued camp armies had always been hired and discharged after crises, others that border forces could not be cut deeply.

sentences.zh: 乃命彥博等詳議以聞。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Yanbo and others to deliberate in detail and report.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yanbo's group to study the matter and report back.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，詔京西路於有糧草州軍招廂軍，共三萬人為額。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year, an edict ordered the Jingxi circuit to recruit Provincial Corps in grain-producing prefectures, with a quota of thirty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In month 7 of Xining 3, Jingxi was told to raise Provincial Corps in grain-rich prefectures, cap thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 十一月，知定州滕甫乞下本路依舊制募弓箭社，以為邊備。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Teng Fu, prefect of Dingzhou, requested that this circuit recruit archer militia companies under the old system for frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: In month 11, Dingzhou prefect Teng Fu asked to restore local archer militia recruitment for border defense.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 四年十二月，樞密院言：“在京係役兵士，舊額一萬八千二百五十九人，見闕六千三百九十二人，若招揀得足，即不須外路勾抽，以免不習水土、凍餒道斃之患。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year, the Bureau reported: "Labor-service troops in the capital had an old quota of 18,259; now 6,392 are short; if recruitment fills the gap, external circuits need not be drawn on, avoiding illness from unfamiliar climate, cold, hunger, and death on the road."
translations.idiomatic: In month 12 of year 4, the Bureau reported capital labor troops were 6,392 below their 18,259 quota; filling them locally would spare men the diseases and deaths of long transfers.

sentences.zh: 欲於在京及府界、京東西、河北招少壯兵，止供在京功役，不許臣僚占差，不過期年，可使充足。

translations.literal: "It is desired to recruit stalwart youths in the capital, capital district, Jingdong, and Hebei for capital labor only, not allowing officials to requisition them, and within one year they can be made full."
translations.idiomatic: They proposed recruiting young men near the capital for capital labor only, barred from official drafts, to reach full strength within a year.

sentences.zh: 卻對減在外招募之數，樁管所減糧賜上供，以給有司之用。”

translations.literal: "Then reduce correspondingly external recruitment, stockpile the reduced grain grants for imperial supply, to fund the ministries' needs."
translations.idiomatic: External recruiting would be cut correspondingly, and saved rations banked for court ministries.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 五年，權發遣延州趙禼招到漢蕃弓箭手人騎四千九百八十四，為八指揮，遂擢吏部員外郎，加賜銀絹二百。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Acting Commissioner Zhao Qi of Yanzhou recruited 4,984 Han and Fan archers and cavalry, organized as eight commands; he was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel and given 200 bolts of silver silk.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5, acting Yanzhou commissioner Zhao Qi raised 4,984 Han and tribal archers in eight commands; he was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel with two hundred bolts of silver silk.

sentences.zh: 七年，分遣使臣諸路選募熙河效用，先以名聞。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, commissioners were sent to circuits to select and recruit Xihe operatives, reporting names first.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7, envoys were sent to circuits to scout and recruit Xihe auxiliaries, names to be reported in advance.

sentences.zh: 河北、河東所募兵悉罷。

translations.literal: Troops recruited in Hebei and Hedong were all disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei and Hedong recruiting was halted entirely.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔軍士祖父母、父母老疾無侍丁而應募在他處者，聽徙。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, an edict: soldiers whose grandparents or parents were old and ill without supporting sons and who had enlisted elsewhere were permitted to transfer.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8, soldiers with aged, ill parents lacking caregivers at home could transfer to posts nearer kin.

sentences.zh: 九年，詔選補捧日、天武以下諸軍闕，馬軍三分補一，步軍十分補五。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, an edict ordered filling vacancies in Pengri, Tianwu, and lower armies: cavalry one in three, infantry five in ten.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9, vacancies in Pengri, Tianwu, and subordinate guards were to be filled at one-third for cavalry and half for infantry.

sentences.zh: 元豐二年二月，經製熙河路邊防財用司言：“岷州┒川、荔川、閭川砦，通遠軍熟羊砦，乞置牧養十監，募兵為監牧指揮。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Yuanfeng, the Frontier Finance Office of the Xihe circuit reported: "At Minzhou Qiongchuan, Lichuan, Lüchuan, and Tongyuan Army Shuyang stockades, request establishing ten pasture supervisors, recruiting troops as pasture-command supervisors."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanfeng-II, the Xihe frontier finance office asked for ten pasture supervisors at Minzhou and Tongyuan stockades, staffed by recruited pasture troops.

sentences.zh: 其營田乞依官莊例，募永濟卒二百人，其永濟卒通以千人為額。”

translations.literal: "For garrison farming, follow the official estate precedent, recruiting two hundred Yongji soldiers; Yongji soldiers in all total one thousand as quota."
translations.idiomatic: For farming they wanted two hundred Yongji soldiers per estate, up to one thousand Yongji troops total.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 七月，沿邊安撫司言：“北邊州軍主管刺事人乞給錢三千，選募使臣職員或百姓為之，以鉤致敵情。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, the frontier pacification office reported: "Northern frontier prefectures' chiefs of tattoo intelligence ask three thousand cash; select and recruit civil or military commissioners or commoners for this, to probe enemy intelligence."
translations.idiomatic: In month 7, border officials asked three thousand cash each for intelligence officers, recruited from officials or civilians to spy on enemies.

sentences.zh: 仍選通判及監官考其虛實，以行賞罰。”

translations.literal: "Also select assistant prefects and supervisory officials to verify truth, applying rewards and punishments."
translations.idiomatic: Assistant prefects and supervisors would verify reports for rewards or penalties.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 是年，以兗、鄆、齊、濟、濱、棣、德、博民饑，募為兵，以補開封府界、京東西將兵之闕。

translations.literal: That year, because Yan, Yun, Qi, Ji, Ji, Bin, Di, De, and Bo had famine, commoners were recruited as troops to fill gaps in the capital district and Jingdong armies.
translations.idiomatic: That year famine in Yan, Yun, Qi, Ji, and other circuits led to recruiting refugees to fill capital and Jingdong unit vacancies.

sentences.zh: 三年，又詔：“府界諸路將下闕禁軍萬數，有司其速募之。”

translations.literal: In the third year, again an edict: "Below the capital district generals, Forbidden Guard vacancies number ten thousand; the ministries should recruit quickly."
translations.idiomatic: In year 3, an edict noted ten thousand capital-region Guard vacancies and ordered rapid filling.

sentences.zh: 又詔：“河北水災，闕食民甚眾，宜寄招補軍。”

translations.literal: Also an edict: "Hebei flood disaster, many lacking food; it is fitting to lodge-recruit and supplement the army."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict directed Hebei flood victims without food into provisional army recruitment.

sentences.zh: 四年，京東、西路以調發兵將，累請增戍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Jingdong East and West circuits, because of dispatching troops, repeatedly requested increased garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4, east and west Jingdong repeatedly asked for more garrison troops after troop deployments.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以兵員有數，多寢其章。

translations.literal: The court, because troop numbers were fixed, mostly shelved their memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The court, holding to fixed troop ceilings, usually ignored these requests.

sentences.zh: 然州郡實有負山帶海，奸盜所窺，亦當過為之慮，其令益廣應募者，與免貼軍及他役一年。

translations.literal: Yet prefectures truly had mountains and sea borders where brigands lurked and should be specially considered; order expanding those willing to enlist, exempting tied-garrison duty and other corvée for one year.
translations.idiomatic: Still, coastal and mountain prefectures faced bandits and deserved consideration: widen recruitment and grant one-year exemptions from tied-garrison duty and other labor duties.

sentences.zh: 六月，詔：“在京奉錢七百以下，選募馬步軍萬五千人；

translations.literal: In the sixth month, an edict: "In the capital, for salary below seven hundred, select and recruit ten thousand five hundred cavalry and infantry;"
translations.idiomatic: In month 6, an edict ordered recruiting 10,500 capital infantry and cavalry among men paid under seven hundred cash.

sentences.zh: 開封府界及本路共選募義兵保甲萬人；

translations.literal: "Capital district and this circuit together select ten thousand righteous militia and baojia;"
translations.idiomatic: The capital district would also raise ten thousand militia and baojia troops.

sentences.zh: 如涇原五千人不足，於秦鳳路選募。”

translations.literal: "if Jingyuan's five thousand are insufficient, select from Qinfeng circuit."
translations.idiomatic: Shortfalls in Jingyuan's five thousand would be made up from Qinfeng.

sentences.zh: 五年五月，同提舉成都府等路茶場蒲宗閔乞自秦州至熙州量地裏遠近險易，置車鋪二十八，招刺兵士。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year, Pu Zongmin, joint commissioner of Chengdu tea stations, requested from Qinzhou to Xizhou measuring distance and difficulty, establishing twenty-eight cart depots and recruiting tattooed soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5-V, tea commissioner Pu Zongmin proposed twenty-eight relay depots from Qinzhou to Xizhou with recruited escort troops.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 八月，詔開封府界、京西招軍依式賜外，仍增錢千。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, an edict: capital district and Jingxi recruitment, beyond standard grants, add one thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: In month 8, recruits in the capital district and Jingxi received an extra thousand cash beyond standard bounty.

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔京城四面巡檢募士於四門，取民年三十五以下者。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, an edict: capital four-side patrol officers recruit men at the four gates, taking commoners thirty-five years or below.
translations.idiomatic: In month 12, capital patrols recruited men under thirty-five at the four city gates.

sentences.zh: 又詔河北立額步軍，各於逐指揮額外招百人。

translations.literal: Also an edict: Hebei established infantry quotas; each command beyond quota recruited one hundred extra men.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei also set infantry quotas, allowing each command one hundred men above establishment.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔一歲內能募及百人者，加秩一等。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict: within one year those able to recruit one hundred men or more received one rank promotion.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5, officers who recruited a hundred men within a year gained one rank.

sentences.zh: 四月，河東路經略司請以麟州飛騎、府州威遠子弟二十五以下剌為兵。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Hedong frontier commissioner requested tattooing as soldiers the Linzhou Feiqi and Fuzhou Weiyuan sons twenty-five years and below.
translations.idiomatic: In month 4, Hedong asked to enlist Linzhou Feiqi and Fuzhou Weiyuan youths under twenty-five.

sentences.zh: 七年，廣西都鈐轄司言：“本路土兵闕額數多，乞選使臣往福建、江南、廣東招簡投換兵四千人。”

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Guangxi commander reported: "This circuit native troops have many quota shortfalls; request selecting commissioners to Fujian, Jiangnan, Guangdong to recruit four thousand exchange soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: In year 7, Guangxi reported large native-troop vacancies and asked to recruit four thousand transfer soldiers from Fujian, Jiangnan, and Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 詔於江南、福建路委官招換。

translations.literal: An edict ordered officials in Jiangnan and Fujian to recruit exchanges.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan and Fujian officials were ordered to conduct transfers.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，河東路安撫使呂惠卿言：“河東敢勇以三百人為額，請給微薄，應募者少。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year, Hedong pacifier Lü Huiqing reported: "Hedong dare-brave troops have a quota of three hundred; stipends are slight and few enlist."
translations.idiomatic: In year 8-IV, Hedong pacifier Lü Huiqing said dare-brave troops, capped at three hundred, drew few recruits because pay was low.

sentences.zh: 臣頃在鄜延路日，奏請增三等請給，借支省馬給七分草料，置營教習，自後應募者眾。

translations.literal: "When I was on the Zhiyan circuit I memorialized to increase stipends three grades, borrow provincial horses at seven-tenths fodder, establish a camp for drill—after that many enlisted."
translations.idiomatic: On Zhiyan he had raised pay three grades, loaned provincial horses at seventy percent fodder, and set up a training camp—after which enrollment surged.

sentences.zh: 願依陝西路已得指揮。”

translations.literal: "I wish to follow the directive already obtained in Shaanxi circuit."
translations.idiomatic: He asked to apply the same Shaanxi rules to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 哲宗元祐元年三月，詔河北保甲願投軍人及得上四軍等杖事藝者，特許招填，合給例物外，更增錢五千，中軍以下三千。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Yuanyou of Zhezong, an edict: Hebei baojia willing to enlist and those meeting Upper Four Armies height and skill were specially permitted to fill vacancies; beyond standard goods, add five thousand cash for Central Army and below three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyou 1-III, Hebei militia volunteers meeting Palace Guard height and skill standards got extra bounties—five thousand cash above Central Army level, three thousand below.

sentences.zh: 比等杖短一指，射保甲第一等弓弩，並許招刺。

translations.literal: Those one finger short on height who shot baojia first-grade bow and crossbow were also permitted tattoo recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: Men one finger short who could draw first-grade militia bows might still enlist.

sentences.zh: 從右司諫蘇轍請也。

translations.literal: This followed Right Remonstrance Su Che's request.
translations.idiomatic: This followed a memorial from Right Remonstrance Su Che.

sentences.zh: 六月，門下侍郎司馬光言：“諸州軍兵馬全欠，不足守禦之處，量與立額招添。”

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Vice Minister of the Gate Sima Guang said: "All circuits' troops and horses are wholly short; where insufficient for defense, measure and set quotas to recruit additions."
translations.idiomatic: In month 6, Vice Minister Sima Guang urged circuits with wholly inadequate garrisons to set quotas and recruit replacements.

sentences.zh: 八年，樞密院言：“今新招兵士多是饑民，未諳教閱，乞自今住營州軍差官訓練，候半年發遣赴軍前。”

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the Bureau reported: "Newly recruited soldiers are mostly famine victims, not versed in drill; from now on posting garrison prefectures should assign officials to train them, and after half a year dispatch to the army front."
translations.idiomatic: In year 8, the Bureau noted new recruits were often famine refugees untrained in drill and asked garrison prefectures to train them six months before front-line deployment.

sentences.zh: 紹聖元年，樞密院乞立招禁軍官員賞格，如不及數，罰亦隨之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaosheng, the Bureau requested setting reward standards for Forbidden Guard recruiters; if below quota, punishments followed.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaosheng 1, the Bureau proposed reward-and-punishment standards for recruitment officers missing quotas.

sentences.zh: 四年，熙河蘭岷路都總管、提點熙河蘭岷等路漢蕃弓箭手司言，蘭州金城關欲招置步軍保捷四指揮、馬軍蕃落一指揮，從之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Xihe Lanmin Commander and Archer Office reported that Lanzhou Jincheng Pass wished to recruit four Baojie infantry commands and one Fanluo cavalry command—approved.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4, the Lanzhou frontier office approved four Baojie infantry and one tribal cavalry command at Jincheng Pass.

sentences.zh: 詔陝西路添置蕃落軍十指揮，各以五百人為額，於永興軍、河中、鳳翔、同、華州各置兩指揮，並隸住營州軍將下統製訓練，委逐路所屬都總管司選官招人。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Shaanxi circuit to add ten Fanluo commands of five hundred each at Yongxing, Hezhong, Fengxiang, Tong, and Hua, two per prefecture, under local generals for training, with the frontier commander selecting recruiters.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi was told to add ten five-hundred-man tribal commands at five prefectures, trained locally and recruited by the frontier commander.

sentences.zh: 初，三省、密院欲以牧地募民牧養馬，久而未集，曾布以謂不若增騎兵為簡便。

translations.literal: Initially the Three Departments and Bureau wished to recruit commoners on pasture land to raise horses, but long without success; Zeng Bu held that increasing cavalry was simpler.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat and Bureau had long tried recruiting herdsmen without success; Zeng Bu argued expanding cavalry was simpler.

sentences.zh: 兼土兵乃勁兵，又諸路出戍者已竭，及建此議，眾翕然皆以為允，帝亦樂從之。

translations.literal: Moreover native troops were stalwart troops, and circuits' expeditionary forces were already exhausted; when this proposal was made, all agreed, and the Emperor also gladly assented.
translations.idiomatic: Native troops were the empire's best fighters, and expeditionary pools were drained; the plan won universal assent, including the emperor's.

sentences.zh: 蓋牧租見存者七百萬，歲額一百七十萬，而十指揮之費二十五萬而已，故可與募人養馬之法兼行也。

translations.literal: For pasture rents in hand totaled seven million, annual income one million seven hundred thousand, while ten commands cost only two hundred fifty thousand—thus it could run alongside hiring commoners to raise horses.
translations.idiomatic: Pasture rents held seven million with 1.7 million annual income, while ten new commands cost only 250,000—so both cavalry expansion and civilian horse programs could coexist.

sentences.zh: 徽宗崇寧元年，湖北都鈐轄舒亶奉旨相度召募施、黔州土丁，致討辰、沅山徭，每州無過七百人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongning of Huizong, Hubei Commander Shu Dan received imperial order to plan recruiting native ding of Shi and Qian prefectures to attack Chen and Yuan mountain Yao, not over seven hundred per prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Huizong's Chongning 1, Hubei commander Shu Dan was ordered to raise Shi and Qian native levies against Yao rebels, capped at seven hundred per prefecture.

sentences.zh: 緣徭賊深在溪洞，險阻不通正軍故也。

translations.literal: Because Yao bandits were deep in stream caves where rugged terrain barred regular troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yao raiders hid in ravines where regular armies could not operate.

sentences.zh: 三年，京東等路招軍五萬，馬軍以崇捷、崇銳名，步軍以崇武、崇威名。

translations.literal: In the third year, Jingdong and other circuits recruited fifty thousand troops; cavalry named Chongjie and Chongrui, infantry Chongwu and Chongwei.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3, Jingdong and other circuits raised fifty thousand troops: cavalry named Chongjie and Chongrui, infantry named Chongwu and Chongwei.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，熙河蘭湟路轉運使洪中孚自河東入覲，帝問崇威、崇銳新兵教閱就緒否。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year, Transit Commissioner Hong Zhongfu of Xihe Lan and Huang came from Hedong to audience; the Emperor asked whether Chongwei and Chongrui new troops' drill was ready.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4-VII, Xihe commissioner Hong Zhongfu, arriving from Hedong, was asked whether the new Chongwei and Chongrui units were drilled.

sentences.zh: 中孚曰：“教閱易事也。

translations.literal: Zhongfu said: "Drill is the easy part."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu replied that drilling them was easy.

sentences.zh: 臣不知藝祖取天下之兵與神考所分將兵曾無減損，若未嚐減損，似不須增。

translations.literal: "Your servant does not know whether the troops with which Founder Taizu took the realm and those Shenzong divided among generals were ever reduced; if never reduced, it seems no increase is needed."
translations.idiomatic: I do not know whether the armies Taizu used to conquer the empire and those Shenzong gave to commanders were ever cut; if not, expansion may be unnecessary.

sentences.zh: 蓋兵貴簡練不貴多，今遽增二軍，所費至廣，臣不知獻議者於經費之外別有措置，或隻仰給朝廷也。”

translations.literal: "For troops value concise training, not numbers; now suddenly adding two armies, the expense is very great—I do not know whether those who proposed this have funds beyond the regular budget, or only look to the court for support."
translations.idiomatic: Armies should be lean, not massive; adding two corps now costs dearly—I wonder whether planners have funding beyond the regular budget or expect the court to pay.

sentences.zh: 帝愕然曰：“初議增兵，未嚐議費，可即罷去。”

translations.literal: The Emperor startled said: "When first discussing increasing troops, never discussed expense—can immediately cancel it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was taken aback. "When we first debated expanding the army, no one talked about cost—call it off at once."

sentences.zh: 中孚曰：“惰遊之卒不復安於南畝，今一旦罷遣，強者聚而為盜，弱者轉徙，則重為朝廷憂。

translations.literal: Zhongfu said: "Idle roving troops will no longer settle at farming in the southern fields; if dismissed at once, the strong will gather as bandits and the weak will wander—then again a heavy worry for the court."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu replied that idle soldiers would not simply return to the fields; if abruptly discharged, strong men would band together as robbers and weak ones would become refugees, creating fresh troubles for the court.

sentences.zh: 不若使填諸營闕；

translations.literal: Better to have them fill vacancies in the various camps;
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to use them to fill vacancies in the camps.

sentences.zh: 無闕，聽於額外收管，不一二年盡矣。”

translations.literal: Where there are no vacancies, allow taking them in beyond the quota—in one or two years they will all be gone.
translations.idiomatic: Where quotas were full, hold the surplus until openings appeared; within a year or two the excess would disappear naturally.

sentences.zh: 帝稱善。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised it as good.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔：“近降指揮，在京、諸路招崇捷、崇武等指揮十萬人，又招效忠、蕃落指揮及額內不足人數，慮卒難敷額，可先招崇捷、崇武十萬人。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, an edict: "Recent orders directed that in the capital and all circuits Chongjie, Chongwu and other commands should recruit one hundred thousand men, and also recruit Xiaozhong, Fanluo commands and shortfalls within quotas; fearing it would be hard to meet quotas at once, Chongjie and Chongwu may first recruit one hundred thousand."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month an edict noted that recent orders had called for recruiting one hundred thousand men into Chongjie, Chongwu, and related commands in the capital and every circuit, along with Xiaozhong and tribal units to cover quota shortfalls. Because filling every slot at once seemed impractical, Chongjie and Chongwu were to raise the first hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 候人數稍見次第，即具申取旨。”

translations.literal: Wait until the numbers gradually show order, then report fully for imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: Once recruitment showed steady progress, officials were to submit a full report for the emperor's decision.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔：“抑勒諸色人投軍者，並許自身及親屬越訴，其已剌字，仍並改正。”

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict: "Those of all categories coerced into military service may appeal for themselves and relatives; those already tattooed shall also have this corrected."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year an edict declared that anyone of any status who had been forced into the army might appeal for himself or his kin, and that men already branded with military tattoos were also to have the matter corrected.

sentences.zh: 政和二年，廣西都鈐司奏：“廣西兩將額一萬三百餘人，事故逃亡，於荊湖南北、江南東西寄招，緣諸路以非本職，多不用心。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenghe, the Guangxi Commander reported: "Guangxi's two generals' quotas total more than ten thousand three hundred; from deaths and desertions, recruitment was delegated to northern and southern Jinghu, eastern and western Jiangnan; because those circuits did not consider it their primary duty, most did not apply themselves."
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 2 the Guangxi command reported that its two generals were authorized more than 10,300 men, but deaths and desertions had forced recruitment onto Jinghu and Jiangnan circuits, where officials treated the work as outside their main duties and gave it little attention.

sentences.zh: 今兵闕六分，欲乞本路、鄰路有犯徒並杖以下情重之人，除配沙門島、廣南遠惡並犯強盜凶惡、殺人放火、事幹化外並依法外，餘並免決刺填。”

translations.literal: Now troops are short six tenths; we wish to request from this circuit and neighboring circuits those guilty of exile and beating offenses of serious circumstances—except those sent to Shamen Island, distant Guangnan, violent robbers, murderers, arsonists, cases involving foreign states and those outside the law—all others exempted from beating and tattooing to fill quotas.
translations.idiomatic: With six tenths of the force now missing, they asked to fill quotas from this circuit and its neighbors by drafting serious offenders sentenced to exile or beating, except men sent to Shamen Island or remote Guangnan, violent robbers, murderers, arsonists, cases touching foreign affairs, and others barred by law; all the rest were to be spared flogging and branding and assigned directly to service.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 四年，中衛大夫童師敏言：“東南州郡例闕廂軍，凡有役使，並是和雇。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Central Guard Grandee Tong Shimin said: "Southeast prefectures and commanderies routinely lack garrison troops; all labor service is hired labor."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Central Guard Grandee Tong Shimin observed that southeastern prefectures usually had no garrison troops and relied on hired labor for every task.

sentences.zh: 若令諸郡守臣並提刑司措置招填，庶可省費。”

translations.literal: If prefectural magistrates and circuit judicial commissioners are all ordered to arrange recruitment to fill quotas, expenses could probably be saved.
translations.idiomatic: If prefects and circuit judicial commissioners were ordered to recruit and fill those quotas, the state might save considerable expense.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 宣和元年，高陽關路安撫使吳玠奉手詔招填諸路禁軍闕額，以十分為率，招及四分以下遞展磨勘年，七分以上遞減磨勘年。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanhe, Gao Yang Pass Circuit Pacification Commissioner Wu Jie received a handwritten edict to recruit and fill forbidden army vacancies on all circuits; using ten parts as the rate, those recruiting four tenths or below would have merit review years extended in succession, seven tenths or above would have merit review years reduced in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 1 Wu Jie, pacification commissioner of the Gaoyang Pass circuit, received a handwritten edict to fill forbidden-army vacancies across the empire. On a scale of ten parts, officials who filled four tenths or less would have their merit-review cycles lengthened step by step, while those reaching seven tenths or more would have them shortened.

sentences.zh: 高陽關路河間府、滄、霸、恩州、信安軍招填數足，乞行推賞。

translations.literal: Gao Yang Pass Circuit Hejian prefecture, Cang, Ba, En prefectures, and Xin'an Army filled recruitment numbers sufficiently and requested commendation rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Hejian, Cang, Ba, En, and the Xin'an Army on the Gaoyang Pass circuit had filled their quotas and asked for promotion rewards.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 二年，手詔：“比聞諸路州軍招置廂軍河清、壯城等，往往怯懦幼小，不及等樣，虛費廩食，不堪驅使。

translations.literal: In the second year, a handwritten edict: "Recently heard that various circuits and garrisons recruiting garrison troops such as River Clearers and Strong City units often take timid, weak, and young men who do not meet standards, wasting grain rations and unfit for service."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year a handwritten edict complained that circuits and garrisons raising garrison units such as river-clearing and wall-guard corps were enrolling timid, undersized youths who failed to meet standards, wasted rations, and could not be put to use.

sentences.zh: 今後並仰遵著令招填，如違戾，以違製論。”

translations.literal: From now on all must follow established regulations for recruitment; if violated, prosecuted as violation of regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth all recruitment was to follow the standing regulations, with violations punished as breaches of imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，兩浙東路鈐轄司奏：“乞將溫、處、衢、婺州元管不係將禁軍六指揮，更招置增為十指揮，並以五百人為額，凡五千人，庶成全將。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, the Eastern Liangzhe Circuit Commander reported: "We request converting Wen, Chu, Qu, and Wu prefectures' original six non-jianjiang forbidden army commands by additional recruitment into ten commands, each with a quota of five hundred, totaling five thousand, so as to complete a full general."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year the Eastern Liangzhe command asked to expand six existing non-jianjiang forbidden-army commands at Wen, Chu, Qu, and Wu into ten commands of five hundred men each, totaling five thousand, so as to complete a full general's force.

sentences.zh: 及更於台州招置不係將禁軍一指揮，以四百人為額。”

translations.literal: And additionally recruit one non-jianjiang forbidden army command at Taizhou, with a quota of four hundred.
translations.idiomatic: They also sought to raise one more non-jianjiang forbidden-army command at Taizhou with a quota of four hundred.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 三月，臣僚言：“竊聞道路洶洶相怖，雲諸軍捉人刺涅以補闕額，率數人驅一壯夫，且曳且毆，百姓叫呼，或齧指求免。

translations.literal: In the third month, officials said: "We privately hear on the roads panic and mutual fear, saying various armies seize people and tattoo them to fill quota shortfalls; several men as a rule drive one strong man, dragging and beating him; commoners cry out, some biting their fingers begging release."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month officials reported widespread panic on the roads: armies were seizing men and branding them to cover quota shortfalls, often with several soldiers dragging and beating one able-bodied man while he screamed and some even bit their fingers begging to be spared.

sentences.zh: 日者，金明池人大和會，忽遮門大索，但長身少年，牽之而去，雲‘充軍’。

translations.literal: Recently at the Jinming Pool great assembly, they suddenly blocked the gates and searched extensively; any tall young man was pulled away, saying 'conscripted for the army.'
translations.idiomatic: At a recent great gathering at Jinming Pool, soldiers suddenly sealed the gates and swept the crowd, hauling off every tall youth they found with the cry that he was being drafted.

sentences.zh: 致賣蔬茹者不敢入城，行旅市人下逮奴隸，皆避藏恐懼，事駭見聞。

translations.literal: This caused vegetable sellers not to dare enter the city; travelers, merchants, and even down to slaves all hid in fear—the matter shocking to witness.
translations.idiomatic: Vegetable sellers stopped entering the city, and travelers, shopkeepers, and even servants hid in terror—a spectacle that horrified all who saw it.

sentences.zh: 今國家閑暇，必欲招填禁旅，當明示法令，賚以金帛，捐財百萬，則十萬人應募矣。

translations.literal: Now the state is at leisure; if it definitely wishes to recruit and fill the forbidden guard, it should clearly announce regulations, reward with gold and silk, and donate wealth of one million—then one hundred thousand would respond to recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was at peace; if the court truly wanted to fill the capital guard, it should publish clear rules, pay generous bounties in gold and silk, and spend a million in cash—then a hundred thousand men would enlist willingly.

sentences.zh: 捉人於途，實虧國體，流聞四方，傳播遠邇，殊為未便。

translations.literal: Seizing people on the road truly damages national dignity; the report spreads to the four directions and is transmitted far and near—extremely inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: Snatching men on the highways truly shamed the state, and word of it spread everywhere, near and far, to the court's great detriment.

sentences.zh: 伏望亟行禁止，以弭疑畏。”

translations.literal: We hope urgently to issue prohibition, to quell suspicion and fear.
translations.idiomatic: They begged the throne to forbid the practice at once and restore public confidence.

sentences.zh: 時寶籙宮道士張繼滋因往尉氏，亦被刺涅，事聞，手詔提刑司根治。

translations.literal: At that time Baolu Palace Daoist priest Zhang Jizi, going to Weishi, was also tattooed; when the matter was reported, a handwritten edict ordered circuit judicial commissioners to investigate thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: About then the Baolu Palace Daoist Zhang Jizi was branded while traveling to Weishi; when the case reached the throne, a handwritten edict ordered the judicial commissioners to investigate it to the full.

sentences.zh: 四月，臣僚因言：“招刺闕額禁軍，樞密院立限太遽，諸營弗戢，人用大駭。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, officials further said: "Recruiting and tattooing forbidden army quota shortfalls—the Bureau of Military Affairs set the deadline too urgent; the camps did not restrain themselves, and the people were greatly frightened."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month officials added that when the Bureau of Military Affairs set overly tight deadlines to tattoo recruits and fill forbidden-army shortfalls, the camps ran wild and the populace was terrified.

sentences.zh: 幸不旋踵德音禁止，群情悅服。

translations.literal: Fortunately, before long an edict of grace prohibited it, and public sentiment was pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately an imperial grace edict soon forbade the practice, and public opinion settled.

sentences.zh: 其已被刺涅而非願者，頗亦改正，尚有經官求免而未得者。

translations.literal: Those already tattooed but unwilling—quite a few had the matter corrected; still there were those who appealed to officials for release but had not yet obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: Many men who had been branded against their will had already been released, though some who had appealed to the authorities were still waiting.

sentences.zh: 輦轂若此，況其遠乎？

translations.literal: If the capital region is like this, how much more so distant places?
translations.idiomatic: If such abuses occurred at the capital, what must be happening in the provinces?

sentences.zh: 竊聞小人假借聲勢，因緣奪攘，所在多有，若或哀鳴得脫，其家已空。

translations.literal: We privately hear petty men borrow authority and seize by opportunity—everywhere there are many; if some cry out pitifully and escape, their family is already emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men everywhere were abusing their power to seize victims, and even when a man escaped after pleading, his household was often already ruined.

sentences.zh: 今往來猶懷畏避。

translations.literal: Now travelers still harbor fear and avoidance.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers still moved about in fear.

sentences.zh: 伏望聖明特賜戒敕，應在外招軍去處，毋得橫濫。”

translations.literal: We hope the sage ruler will specially grant a warning edict: at all places outside recruiting troops, they must not exceed bounds.
translations.idiomatic: They asked the emperor to issue a special warning that recruiting parties in the provinces must not exceed their authority.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 七年，減掖庭用度，減侍從官以上月廩，罷諸兼局，有司據所得數撥充諸路糴本及募兵賞軍之用。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Inner Palace expenses were reduced, monthly stipends of attendants and above were reduced, various concurrent bureaus were abolished, and departments allocated the amounts obtained for grain purchase capital on all circuits and recruit-troop reward funds.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the court cut Inner Palace spending, reduced the monthly stipends of attendants and higher officials, abolished concurrent bureaus, and directed the savings toward grain-purchase funds and recruitment bounties on the circuits.

sentences.zh: 欽宗即位，詔守令募州縣鄉村土豪為隊長，各自募其親識鄉里以行。

translations.literal: When Qinzong acceded, an edict ordered magistrates to recruit local gentry of prefectures, counties, and villages as squad leaders, each recruiting acquaintances from his home district to go forth.
translations.idiomatic: When Qinzong took the throne, he ordered magistrates to enlist local strongmen as squad leaders, each to raise men from his own neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 及五十人以上先與進義副尉，三百人以上與承信郎，募文武官習武勇者為統領。

translations.literal: Those reaching fifty or more were first given Jin Yi Vice Wei rank; three hundred or more were given Cheng Xin Lang; civil and military officials skilled in martial arts and bravery were recruited as commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Leaders who raised fifty men received the rank of Advance Righteousness Vice Commander, and those who raised three hundred received Trustworthy Gentleman; civil and military officials versed in arms were recruited as unit commanders.

sentences.zh: 行日，所發州軍授以器甲，人給糧半月，地裏遠者，所至州縣接續批支。

translations.literal: On the day of departure, the issuing prefecture or army gave arms and armor; each man received half a month of rations; for distant places, prefectures and counties en route continued issuing them.
translations.idiomatic: On the day they marched, the issuing prefecture or garrison supplied arms and armor and half a month's rations, with counties along the route continuing payment for men coming from far away.

sentences.zh: 京畿輔郡兵馬製置使司言：“諸路召募敢勇效用，每名先給錢三千，赴本司試驗給據訖，支散銀絹激賞。

translations.literal: The Capital Region Pacification Bureau said: "All circuits recruiting dare-brave effective troops—each man first given three thousand cash, comes to this bureau for testing and certification, then silver and silk rewards are distributed."
translations.idiomatic: The Capital Region Pacification Bureau reported that dare-brave volunteers recruited on the circuits were to receive three thousand cash in advance, then report to the bureau for testing and certification before receiving silver and silk bonuses.

sentences.zh: 若監司、知通、令佐並應有官人，能召到敢勇效用事藝高強及二百人以上者，乞與轉一官，每加二百人依此。

translations.literal: If surveillance commissioners, prefects, county magistrates, and all relevant officials can recruit two hundred or more highly skilled dare-brave effective troops, we request one rank promotion; for each additional two hundred, the same applies.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who raised two hundred or more skilled dare-brave volunteers were to receive one rank of promotion, with the same reward for every additional two hundred.

sentences.zh: 或監司、郡守、州縣官以下應緣軍期事件，稍有稽緩，並依軍法。”

translations.literal: Or if surveillance commissioners, prefects, and county officials and below regarding military deadline matters are slightly delayed, all are subject to military law.
translations.idiomatic: Any surveillance commissioner, prefect, or county official who delayed matters tied to the military deadline would be punished under military law.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年春正月，臣僚言：“諸路見招募人兵，緣逐處漕計闕乏，乞於近州應奉司及延福宮西城錢帛，並許請用，庶得速辦。”

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the first year of Jingkang, officials said: "All circuits are now recruiting troops; because each place's transport commission funds are lacking, we request that nearby prefectures' imperial tribute offices and Yanfu Palace west city money and silk all be permitted for use, so that completion may be speeded."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Jingkang 1 officials noted that circuits were recruiting troops but local transport offices lacked funds, and asked permission to draw on nearby imperial tribute stores and the Yanfu Palace treasury in the west city so recruitment could proceed quickly.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 又詔：“龍猛、龍騎、歸遠、壯勇諸軍闕額，可行下諸路揀選配填。”

translations.literal: Another edict: "Dragon Fierce, Dragon Cavalry, Return Far, Strong Brave and other armies' quota shortfalls may be issued to all circuits for selection and assignment to fill."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict ordered circuits to select men to fill vacancies in the Dragon Fierce, Dragon Cavalry, Return Far, Strong Brave, and related corps.

sentences.zh: 又詔：“已降指揮，逐處各以召募效用敢勇武藝人數多寡等第推賞。”

translations.literal: Another edict: "According to previously issued orders, each place shall recommend rewards by grade according to the numbers of effective dare-brave martial recruits recruited."
translations.idiomatic: A further edict directed each locality to recommend rewards by rank according to how many skilled dare-brave volunteers it had raised under earlier orders.

sentences.zh: 又詔：“聞希賞之人，抑勒強募。

translations.literal: Another edict: "We hear that those hoping for rewards coercively force recruitment."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict noted that men seeking promotion rewards were forcibly pressing recruits into service.

sentences.zh: 自今並取情願，敢有違戾，當議重罰。

translations.literal: From now on all shall take willing consent; if anyone violates, heavy punishment shall be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth only willing volunteers were to be accepted, and violators would face severe punishment.

sentences.zh: 毋得將羸弱不堪出戰及已有係軍籍者一例充募。”

translations.literal: Must not take the weak and unfit for battle and those already on military registers and treat them the same as recruits.
translations.idiomatic: Weak men unfit for combat and men already registered in the army were not to be enrolled indiscriminately.

sentences.zh: 及詔：“募武舉及第有材武方略，或有戰功、曾經戰陣，及經邊任大小使臣不以罪犯已發未敘，及武學有方略智謀，及曾充弓馬所子弟，及諸色有膽勇敢戰之人，度許赴親征行營司。”

translations.literal: And an edict: "Recruit military examination jinshi with talent, martial arts, and strategy, or those with battle merit who have seen the battlefield, frontier commissioners large and small regardless of whether crimes have been committed or not yet disposed, martial academy students with strategy and wisdom, former bow-and-horse institute students, and men of all categories with courage who dare fight—permit them to go to the Personal Campaign Headquarters."
translations.idiomatic: An edict also called for recruiting military examination graduates with proven talent and strategy, men with battle honors or field experience, frontier commissioners regardless of pending criminal cases, martial academy students of proven wit, former bow-and-horse institute trainees, and all other brave fighters willing to serve, and allowing them to report to the Personal Campaign Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 又詔：“募陝西土人為兵並使臣、效用等赴姚平仲軍使喚，其應募人修武郎已上二十貫，進義副尉以上十五貫，軍人、百姓十貫，並於開封府應管官錢內支。”

translations.literal: Another edict: "Recruit Shaanxi locals as soldiers and commissioners, effective troops, and the like to Yao Pingzhong's army for summons; recruits of Xi Wu Lang and above receive twenty strings, Jin Yi Vice Wei and above fifteen strings, soldiers and commoners ten strings—all disbursed from Kaifeng prefecture's managed official funds."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict ordered Shaanxi locals, commissioners, and volunteers to report to Yao Pingzhong's army, with recruits paid twenty strings if ranked Xi Wu Lang or higher, fifteen strings if Jin Yi Vice Commander or higher, and ten strings for soldiers and commoners, all from Kaifeng's official treasury.

sentences.zh: 四月，詔：“已降指揮發還歸朝人往大金軍前，如不願往，所在量給口券津遣；

translations.literal: In the fourth month, an edict: "According to previously issued orders, send back those returning to court toward the Great Jin army front; if unwilling to go, each place shall measure and give travel vouchers for repatriation;"
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month an edict ordered envoys returning from the Jin front to proceed as previously directed, but allowed men who refused to be issued travel vouchers and sent home.

sentences.zh: 元有官守人並不厘務，支奉給之半。

translations.literal: Original officeholders shall all suspend duties and receive half stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who held posts were to suspend their duties and receive half pay.

sentences.zh: 其願效力軍前者，許自陳。”

translations.literal: Those willing to serve at the army front are permitted to declare themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Men willing to serve at the front were permitted to volunteer.

sentences.zh: 五月，河北、河東路宣撫司奏：“河北諸州軍所管正兵絕少，又陝西遊手惰民願充軍者亦眾，祗緣招刺闕乏例物，是致軍額常闕。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the Hebei and Hedong Pacification Bureau memorialized: "Hebei prefectures and garrisons have extremely few regular troops under their charge; moreover many idle drifting people in Shaanxi are willing to serve—as only because recruitment tattooing lacks standard gifts, army quotas are constantly short."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Hebei-Hedong Pacification Bureau reported that Hebei garrisons held very few regular troops, while many idle men in Shaanxi were willing to enlist, but quotas stayed unfilled because standard enlistment gifts were lacking.

sentences.zh: 今若給一色銀絹，折充例物犒設起發，召募人作義勇，止於右臂上刺字，依禁軍例物支衣糧料錢，陝西五路共可得二萬人，比之淮、浙等路所得將兵，實可使喚。”

translations.literal: Now if uniform silver and silk are given, converted to standard gifts for feasts and departure costs, recruits are enlisted as Righteous Braves with tattooing only on the right arm, and clothing, grain, and ration money paid per forbidden army standards, Shaanxi's five circuits together can obtain twenty thousand—compared with general troops obtained from Huai and Zhe circuits, they can truly be put to use.
translations.idiomatic: If the court paid enlistment bounties in silver and silk, raised the men as Righteous Braves with a tattoo only on the right arm, and supplied clothing and rations at forbidden-army rates, Shaanxi's five circuits could furnish twenty thousand men far more useful than the general troops raised in Huai and Zhe.

sentences.zh: 從之，詔遣文武官各一員前去陝西路募兵二萬人赴闕。

translations.literal: Approved; an edict dispatched one civil and one military official each to Shaanxi circuit to recruit twenty thousand troops to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved, and the throne sent one civil and one military official to Shaanxi to raise twenty thousand men for the capital.

sentences.zh: 遂命趙鼎特除開封府曹官，種湘差宣撫司準備將領，並充陝西路幹當公事，專一募兵。

translations.literal: Zhao Ding was then specially appointed Kaifeng prefecture clerk, and Zhong Xiang was assigned as Pacification Bureau reserve general; both served as Shaanxi circuit duty officers exclusively recruiting troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ding was specially appointed a Kaifeng prefectural clerk and Zhong Xiang a reserve general on the pacification staff, both assigned to Shaanxi solely to handle recruitment.

sentences.zh: 是月，遣戶部員外郎陳師尹往福建路募槍杖手。

translations.literal: That month, Household Ministry Vice Director Chen Shiyin was dispatched to Fujian circuit to recruit spear and staff fighters.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Household Vice Director Chen Shiyin was sent to Fujian to recruit spearmen and staff fighters.

sentences.zh: 都水使者陳求道言：“朝廷差官往陝西招軍，適當歲豐，恐未易招填。

translations.literal: Director of Waterways Chen Qiudao said: "The court dispatched officials to Shaanxi to recruit troops—just when the harvest is abundant; I fear it will not be easy to fill quotas."
translations.idiomatic: Director of Waterways Chen Qiudao warned that officials sent to Shaanxi to raise troops had arrived during a bumper harvest, when recruitment would be difficult.

sentences.zh: 若就委監司招募保甲，啖以例物，與免科差，以作其氣，可得勁兵五萬。”

translations.literal: If surveillance commissioners are entrusted to recruit baojia, enticed with standard gifts and exempted from corvée levies to rouse their spirit, fifty thousand strong troops can be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: If surveillance commissioners were instead told to mobilize the baojia militia with enlistment gifts and corvée exemptions to stir their morale, fifty thousand strong fighters could be raised.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 六月，樞密都承旨折彥實奏：“西人結連女真，為日甚久，豈無覬覦關中之誌？

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Bureau Chief Zhe Yanshi memorialized: "Western people have allied with the Jurchen for a long time—how can they not covet Guanzhong?"
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Bureau Chief Zhe Yanshi warned that the western peoples had long been allied with the Jurchen and surely harbored designs on Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 即今諸路人馬皆空，萬一敵人長驅，何以枝梧？

translations.literal: Now men and horses on all circuits are empty—if the enemy charges deep, how can we resist?
translations.idiomatic: Every circuit was now stripped of troops and horses; if the enemy drove deep into the realm, how could the court hold them off?

sentences.zh: 言之可為寒心，朝廷似未深慮也。

translations.literal: Speaking of it makes one cold-hearted; the court seems not to have deeply considered it.
translations.idiomatic: The thought was chilling, yet the court seemed not to have weighed it seriously.

sentences.zh: 河東、河塑之患已形，人故憂之；

translations.literal: The troubles of Hedong and the Hedong region crisis have already taken shape, so people therefore worry;
translations.idiomatic: The crisis in the Hedong region has already become visible, and the people are anxious;

sentences.zh: 陝西之患未作，人故忽之。

translations.literal: The trouble in Shaanxi has not yet begun, so people therefore neglect it.
translations.idiomatic: the danger in Shaanxi had not yet materialized, so people ignored it.

sentences.zh: 若每路先與十萬緡，令帥臣招募土人為保護之計，責以控扼，不得放令侵入，仍須朝廷應副。

translations.literal: If each circuit is first given one hundred thousand strings, circuit commanders are ordered to recruit locals as a protection plan, charged with controlling and blocking and not allowing invasion, the court must still provide support.
translations.idiomatic: If each circuit were given one hundred thousand strings upfront and its commander ordered to recruit local men for defense, hold the passes, and bar enemy entry, the court would still have to back the effort.

sentences.zh: 漕司乘時廣行儲蓄，以為急務。”

translations.literal: Transport commissioners should seize the time to store provisions broadly, taking this as an urgent task.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioners should urgently build up grain reserves while there was still time.

sentences.zh: 又開封府尹聶山奏：“招兵者，今日之急務。

translations.literal: Kaifeng Prefect Nie Shan also memorialized: "Recruiting troops is today's urgent task."
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng Prefect Nie Shan also submitted that raising troops was the day's most urgent business.

sentences.zh: 近緣京畿諸邑例各招刺，至於無人就募，則強捕村民及往來行人為之。

translations.literal: Recently because counties of the capital region each routinely recruit and tattoo—to the point that when no one enlists, they forcibly capture villagers and travelers passing by.
translations.idiomatic: Recently every county around the capital had taken to branding recruits, and when no one volunteered they seized villagers and travelers off the roads.

sentences.zh: 遂致裏氓奔駭，商旅不行，殊失朝廷愛民之意。

translations.literal: Thus causing inner residents to flee in panic and merchants not to travel—greatly losing the court's intent to love the people.
translations.idiomatic: Country folk fled in panic and merchants stopped traveling, a gross betrayal of the court's duty to protect the people.

sentences.zh: 檢準政和令，諸盜再犯杖以上、情理不可決放而堪充軍者，給例物刺充廂軍。

translations.literal: Checking against the Zhenghe regulations: repeat thieves sentenced to beating or above, whose circumstances cannot be released by judgment but who are fit for army service, are given standard gifts and tattooed as garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhenghe code, repeat thieves sentenced to flogging or worse who could not be released but were fit for service were to receive enlistment gifts and be branded into garrison corps.

sentences.zh: 今京城裏外間有盜賊，皆是豪猾，無所畏憚，雖經斷罪，頑惡弗悛，若依上條刺充廂軍，不惟得強壯之用，又且收集奸黠不復為盜。

translations.literal: Now inside and outside the capital there are occasionally bandits—all bold and cunning, fearless; though sentenced, stubborn and unrepentant; if per the above rule they are tattooed as garrison troops, not only will strong men be obtained for use, but cunning men will also be gathered and no longer become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Bold, hardened thieves still prowled inside and outside the capital; though convicted, they remained unreformed. Drafting them into garrison service under that rule would not only supply strong recruits but also sweep the worst offenders off the streets.

sentences.zh: 如允所請，則自內及外皆可見之施行。”

translations.literal: If the request is approved, then from inside to outside all can see it implemented.
translations.idiomatic: If approved, the policy could be applied from the capital outward for all to see.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 七月，陝西五路製置使錢蓋言：“都水使者陳求道請招刺保甲五萬充軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Shaanxi Five Circuits Commissioner Qian Gai said: "Director of Waterways Chen Qiudao requests recruiting and tattooing fifty thousand baojia as soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Shaanxi Five-Circuit Commissioner Qian Gai reported that Director of Waterways Chen Qiudao had proposed branding fifty thousand baojia militiamen into regular service.

sentences.zh: 緣比來陝右正兵數少，全籍保甲守禦，及運糧諸役差使外，所餘無幾，若更招刺五萬充軍，則是正丁占使殆遍，不唯難以選擇，兼慮民情驚疑，別致生事。

translations.literal: Because recently regular troops on the Shaanxi right are few, defense relies entirely on baojia; apart from transport grain and various corvée assignments, the remainder is few—if another fifty thousand are recruited and tattooed as soldiers, then prime males for service are nearly all used; not only will selection be difficult, but popular sentiment may be alarmed and cause other troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Regular troops in western Shaanxi were already scarce and local defense depended entirely on the baojia; after grain transport and corvée duties almost no able men remained. Drafting fifty thousand more would leave few prime males to choose from, alarm the populace, and invite unrest.

sentences.zh: 欲乞令州縣曉諭保甲，取其情願；

translations.literal: We wish to request ordering prefectures and counties to instruct baojia and take their willing consent;
translations.idiomatic: He asked that prefectures and counties explain the plan to the baojia and accept only volunteers;

sentences.zh: 如未有情願之人，即乞令保甲司於正丁餘數內選擇。

translations.literal: if there are no willing persons, then request ordering the baojia bureau to select from the surplus of prime males.
translations.idiomatic: and if too few volunteered, that the baojia office choose men from the remaining pool of prime males.

sentences.zh: 通赴闕人共成七萬，可以足用。”

translations.literal: Total men going to the capital together making seventy thousand can be sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Together with men already bound for the capital, seventy thousand would be enough.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 是月，錢蓋奏：“陝西募土人充軍，多是市井烏合，不堪臨敵。

translations.literal: That month, Qian Gai memorialized: "Shaanxi recruiting locals as soldiers—most are market rabble, unfit to face the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: That month Qian Gai reported that locals recruited in Shaanxi were mostly urban rabble unfit to face the enemy.

sentences.zh: 今折彥實支陝西六路銅錢各十萬緡，每名添錢十千，自可精擇少壯及等杖人，可得正軍一萬，六路共得六萬人。”

translations.literal: Now Zhe Yanshi disburses to Shaanxi's six circuits copper cash of one hundred thousand strings each; adding ten thousand cash per man, one can carefully select young strong men meeting standards—ten thousand regular troops can be obtained, six circuits together sixty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: If Zhe Yanshi allocated one hundred thousand strings of copper cash to each of Shaanxi's six circuits and added ten thousand cash per recruit, the state could carefully select able young men meeting standards and raise ten thousand regular soldiers per circuit, sixty thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 十月，樞密院奏：“召募有材武勇銳及膽勇人並射獵射生戶。”

translations.literal: In the tenth month, the Bureau of Military Affairs memorialized: "Recruit men with talent, martial arts, sharpness, and courage, also hunting and hunting-for-living households."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Bureau of Military Affairs proposed recruiting men of proven martial skill and courage, including hunters and professional hunting households.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 又奏：“福建路有忠義武勇立功自效取仕之人，理宜召募，除保甲正兵外，弓手、百姓、僧行、有罪軍人並聽應募。

translations.literal: It also memorialized: "Fujian circuit has loyal, righteous, martial, brave men seeking office through merit—properly they should be recruited; except baojia regular troops, archers, commoners, monks, and guilty soldiers are all permitted to enlist."
translations.idiomatic: It also proposed recruiting in Fujian men of loyal spirit and martial merit who sought office through service, allowing archers, commoners, monks, and even convicted soldiers to enlist alongside the baojia regulars.

sentences.zh: 如有武藝高強、實有膽勇、眾所推服、願應募為部領人者，依逐項名目權攝部領，各以所募人數借補官資。”

translations.literal: If there are men of high martial skill, truly courageous, universally respected, and willing to enlist as unit leaders, they shall temporarily act as leaders according to each item's title, each temporarily supplementing official rank according to the number recruited.
translations.idiomatic: Men of outstanding skill and recognized courage who volunteered to lead were to serve temporarily as unit commanders and receive provisional rank according to the number they raised.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 十一月，京城四壁共十萬人，黃人黃旗滿市。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the four walls of the capital totaled one hundred thousand men; yellow-clad men and yellow banners filled the markets.
translations.idiomatic: By the eleventh month a hundred thousand defenders manned the capital's four walls, and yellow-clad troops with yellow banners filled the streets.

sentences.zh: 時應募者多庸匄，殊無鬥誌。

translations.literal: At the time many who answered the call were idle beggars, utterly without fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Most who enlisted were vagrants and beggars with no will to fight.

sentences.zh: 閏十一月，何㮚用王健募奇兵，雖操瓢行乞之人，亦皆應募，倉卒未就紀律。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eleventh month, He Li had Wang Jian recruit irregular troops; even men who carried ladles and begged for a living all enrolled, and in haste discipline had not been established.
translations.idiomatic: In intercalary November He Li put Wang Jian in charge of raising irregular troops; even ladle-carrying beggars enlisted, and the unit was hurriedly assembled without proper discipline.

sentences.zh: 奇兵亂，毆王健，殺使臣數十人，內前大擾。

translations.literal: The irregular troops mutinied, beat Wang Jian, killed several tens of envoys, and the Inner Front was greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: The irregulars mutinied, assaulted Wang Jian, and slew dozens of court agents, throwing the Inner Front into chaos.

sentences.zh: 王宗濋斬渠魁數人，乃定。

translations.literal: Wang Zongsu executed several ringleaders, then order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongsu beheaded several ringleaders and restored order.

sentences.zh: 及出戰，為鐵騎所衝，望風奔潰，殲焉。

translations.literal: When they went out to battle, they were struck by iron cavalry, fled and broke at sight of the enemy, and were annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: Sent into battle, they were overrun by heavy cavalry, broke and fled at first shock, and were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔：“諸軍詐效蕃裝，焚劫財物，限十日齎贓自首，與免罪。”

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, an edict: "All armies who falsely disguise themselves in barbarian dress and burn and plunder goods — within ten days bring stolen goods and surrender themselves, and pardon shall be granted."
translations.idiomatic: In December an edict declared that any troops who masqueraded as Jurchen raiders to loot would receive amnesty if they returned stolen goods and surrendered within ten days.

sentences.zh: 仍召募潰兵收管。

translations.literal: Routed soldiers were also to be recruited and taken into custody.
translations.idiomatic: Routed soldiers were also to be collected and registered.

sentences.zh: 給口食焉。

translations.literal: Provisions were to be issued to them.
translations.idiomatic: They were to receive rations.

sentences.zh: 逃亡之法，國初以來各有增損。

translations.literal: Laws on desertion since the founding of the dynasty had each been revised with additions and subtractions.
translations.idiomatic: Desertion laws had been revised repeatedly since the dynasty's founding.

sentences.zh: 熙寧五年詔，禁軍奉錢至五百而亡滿七日者，斬。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xining, an edict: Palace Guards whose monthly stipend reached five hundred cash and who deserted for a full seven days — execution.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 5 an edict decreed execution for Palace Guards on the five-hundred-cash pay grade who remained absent seven full days.

sentences.zh: 舊制，三日者死。

translations.literal: Under the former regulation, three days meant death.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rule, three days' absence meant death.

sentences.zh: 初，執政議更法，請滿十日。

translations.literal: Initially the chief ministers discussed changing the law and requested a full ten days.
translations.idiomatic: At first the chief ministers proposed reform and asked that the limit be ten days.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“臨陣而亡，過十日而首，得不長奸乎。”

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Deserting in the face of battle — if after ten days one turns oneself in, will this not encourage wickedness?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor objected: "Men who flee during combat could still surrender after ten days — would that not reward cowardice?"

sentences.zh: 安石曰：“臨陣而亡，法不計日，即入斬刑。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi said: "Deserting in battle — the law does not count days; it immediately incurs the death penalty."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi replied that desertion in battle already carried immediate execution regardless of days counted.

sentences.zh: 今當立在軍興所亡滿三日，論如對寇賊律？”

translations.literal: Now ought we establish that desertion for a full three days at a place of military mobilization be judged under the law for facing enemy bandits?
translations.idiomatic: Should we instead treat three days' absence during mobilization as desertion against the enemy, under the bandit-combat statute?

sentences.zh: 樞密使蔡挺請沿邊而亡滿三日者斬。

translations.literal: The Military Affairs Commissioner Cai Ting requested that along the frontier, deserters absent a full three days be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Military Affairs Commissioner Cai Ting urged that frontier deserters absent three full days be beheaded.

sentences.zh: 安石曰：“沿邊有非軍興之所，不可一概坐以重刑。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi said: "Along the frontier there are places that are not sites of military mobilization; one cannot uniformly impose heavy punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi countered that the frontier included many posts not under wartime mobilization, and heavy penalties could not be applied uniformly.

sentences.zh: 本立重法，以禁避寇賊及軍興而已。”

translations.literal: The original purpose of establishing severe law was merely to forbid evading enemy bandits and military mobilization.
translations.idiomatic: The harsh law had been meant only to deter men from fleeing the enemy or wartime service.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“然。”

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "So it is."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 文彥博固言：“軍法臣等所當總領，不宜輕改，如前代銷兵乃生變。”

translations.literal: Wen Yanbo obstinately said: "Military law is what we ministers ought to oversee; it should not be lightly changed — as in earlier dynasties when reducing troops produced mutiny."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo insisted that military law was the ministers' charge and should not be altered lightly, warning that past troop reductions had sparked uprisings.

sentences.zh: 安石曰：“前代如杜元穎等銷兵，乃其措置失當，非兵不可銷也。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi said: "In earlier dynasties such as Du Yuanying reducing troops — it was their mishandling; it is not that troops cannot be reduced."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi answered that disasters like Du Yuanying's demobilization stemmed from poor execution, not from demobilization itself.

sentences.zh: 且當蕭俛時，天下兵至多，民力不給，安得不減？

translations.literal: Moreover at the time of Xiao Fu, troops under Heaven were exceedingly many and civilian strength could not supply them — how could reduction not occur?
translations.idiomatic: Under Chancellor Xiao Fu the empire had fielded more soldiers than the populace could support — reduction had been unavoidable.

sentences.zh: 方幽州以朱克融等送京師，請毋遣克融還幽州煽眾為亂，而朝廷乃令克融等飄泊京師，久之不調，復遣歸北。

translations.literal: Just when Youzhou sent Zhu Kerong and others to the capital and requested that Kerong not be sent back to Youzhou to incite the masses to rebellion, the court nevertheless left Kerong and others adrift in the capital, long without appointment, then sent them back north again.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhou sent Zhu Kerong and others to court with a plea not to return Kerong lest he stir rebellion in the north, the court instead kept them stranded in the capital, left them unassigned for years, and then sent them home again.

sentences.zh: 克融所以復亂，亦何預銷兵事？”

translations.literal: Therefore Kerong's renewed rebellion — what has it to do with reducing troops?
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Kerong's renewed revolt had nothing to do with troop reduction.

sentences.zh: 彥博曰：“國初，禁軍逃亡滿一日者斬。

translations.literal: Yanbo said: "At the founding of the dynasty, forbidden-army deserters absent a full day were executed."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo cited the founding-era rule that Palace Guard deserters gone even one day were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 仁宗改滿三日，當時議者已慮壞軍法。”
