translations.literal: Emperor Renzong changed it to a full three days; discussants at the time already worried this would ruin military law.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong had extended the limit to three days, and critics even then feared it would erode discipline.

sentences.zh: 安石曰：“仁宗改法以來，活人命至多，然於軍人逃亡，比舊不聞加多，仁宗改法不為不善。”

translations.literal: Wang Anshi said: "Since Emperor Renzong changed the law, lives spared have been exceedingly many; yet as for military men deserting, compared with old times one does not hear of increase — Renzong's legal change was not unwise."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi replied that Renzong's reform had saved countless lives without any evident rise in desertions — it had been a sound change.

sentences.zh: 帝乃詔增為七日。

translations.literal: The Emperor then issued an edict to increase it to seven days.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the limit raised to seven days.

sentences.zh: 元豐元年，知鄂州王韶言：“乞自今逃亡配軍為盜，聽捕斬，賞錢。”

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyong, Ezhou prefect Wang Shao said: "I request that from now on convict-soldiers who desert and become bandits may be captured and executed, with reward money."
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyong 1 Wang Shao, prefect of Ezhou, proposed allowing deserter-convicts turned bandits to be killed on capture, with a bounty offered.

sentences.zh: 詔坐條劄韶照會：“如所犯情重，罪不至死，奏裁。”

translations.literal: An edict established a provision memorializing Shao's note: "If the circumstances of the offense are serious but the crime does not reach death, memorialize for imperial decision."
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied with a formal note to Shao: offenses grave yet short of capital punishment were to be referred for imperial review.

sentences.zh: 三年六月，詔：“軍士、民兵逃亡隨軍效用，若首獲，並械送所屬，論如法。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year, an edict: "Soldiers and militia who desert and follow the army as volunteers — if first captured, all shall be shackled and sent to their units and judged according to law."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year 3 an edict required that deserters who rejoined as volunteers be shackled and returned to their commands for punishment under the statutes.

sentences.zh: 雖立戰功不賞，仍不許以功贖過。

translations.literal: Even if they establish battle merit, no reward; still not permitted to redeem faults with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Battle honors would not be rewarded, and merit could not expiate the offense.

sentences.zh: 令隨軍榜諭。”

translations.literal: The order was to be posted in proclamation with the army.
translations.idiomatic: The order was to be posted throughout the campaign camps.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔沈括：“奏以軍前士卒逃亡，潰散在路，本非得已，須當急且招安。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict to Shen Kuo: "Memorialize that soldiers before the army who desert, routed and scattered on the roads, did not do so without cause; one must urgently recruit and pacify them for now."
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 the throne instructed Shen Kuo to report that front-line deserters scattered along the roads had often fled from necessity and should be pacified at once.

sentences.zh: 卿可速具朝旨出榜，雲聞戰士止是不禁饑寒，逃歸其家，可各隨所在城砦權送納器甲，請給糧食，聽歸所屬。

translations.literal: You should quickly prepare the court's intent and issue a proclamation, declaring that it is heard warriors merely could not endure hunger and cold and fled home — each may at local walled posts temporarily turn in weapons and armor, request grain rations, and be permitted to return to their units.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Kuo was to issue a proclamation explaining that men had fled chiefly from hunger and cold, allowing them to surrender arms at nearby posts, draw rations, and rejoin their commands.

sentences.zh: 節次具招撫數以聞。”

translations.literal: Successively report the numbers pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He was to report recovery totals as they came in.

sentences.zh: 崇寧四年九月，樞密院言：“熙河都總管司舊無兵籍，乞令諸將各置籍，日具有無開收，旬具元額、見管及逃亡事故細目，申總管司，本司揭貼都簿，委機宜一員逐時抽摘點檢。”

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Chongning, the Bureau of Military Affairs said: "The Xihe Commander-in-Chief's office formerly had no troop registers — I request that each general establish registers, daily record additions and subtractions, every ten days record original quota, currently managed, and desertion incident details and report to the Commander office; this office shall post the general ledger and delegate one staff officer to conduct spot checks at intervals."
translations.idiomatic: In Chongning 4, ninth month, the Bureau of Military Affairs noted that the Xihe headquarters lacked roster records and asked each commander to keep daily strength accounts, submit ten-day reports on quotas and desertions, post a master ledger, and assign an aide for spot inspections.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 十月，尚書省言：“今所在逃軍聚集，至以千數，小則驚動鄉邑，大則公為劫盜。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, the Ministry of Revenue said: "Now deserters gather everywhere, reaching into the thousands; small groups startle townships, large ones openly become bandits."
translations.idiomatic: In October the Ministry of Revenue reported that deserters were gathering by the thousands, terrorizing villages or turning openly to robbery.

sentences.zh: 累降指揮，許以首身，或令投換，終未革絕。

translations.literal: Repeatedly issued orders permitting self-surrender or transfer and reassignment — still not eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated amnesties allowing surrender or transfer had failed to stop the problem.

sentences.zh: 昔神宗以將不知兵，兵不知將，故分兵領將。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Shenzong, because generals did not know troops and troops did not know generals, thus divided troops and assigned generals.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong had separated command from troops precisely because officers and men did not know each other.

sentences.zh: 統兵官司，凡兵之事無所不統，則其逃亡走死，豈得不任其責？

translations.literal: Command agencies that oversee all military affairs — when deserters flee and die, how can they not bear responsibility?
translations.idiomatic: Commands charged with every aspect of troop welfare surely bore responsibility for desertion and death in service.

sentences.zh: 檢會將敕與見行敕令，皆未有將官與人員任責之法，致令來兵將不加存恤，勞役其身，至於逃避，而任職之人悉不加罪。

translations.literal: Reviewing general orders and current statutes, none had methods assigning responsibility to commanders and clerks, causing incoming officers not to care for troops, overworking them until they fled, while incumbent officials all went unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: Neither regulations nor active code assigned accountability to commanders and staff, so officers overworked their men until they deserted while responsible officials went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 近日熙河一路逃者幾四萬，將副坐視而不禁，人員將校故縱而不問，至逃亡軍人所在皆有。

translations.literal: Recently on the Xihe route deserters nearly reached forty thousand; deputy generals sat watching without restraining, clerks and company officers deliberately indulged without inquiry — deserters were everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly forty thousand men had recently deserted in Xihe alone, while deputies looked on, staff winked, and fugitives filled the countryside.

sentences.zh: 蓋自來立法未詳，兼軍中長行節級人員，將校，什長相統，同營相依，上下相製，豈得致其逃亡漫不省察？

translations.literal: Surely because legislation from the start was not detailed, and also army regulars in rank, clerks, company officers, and squad leaders oversee one another, same camp depend on each other, upper and lower restrain each other — how could they bring about desertion and pay no attention?
translations.idiomatic: Vague laws and a chain of squad leaders, officers, and clerks bound to the same camp made unchecked desertion inexcusable.

sentences.zh: 況招軍既立賞格，則逃走安可無禁？

translations.literal: Moreover since recruiting troops has established reward standards, how can fleeing go unpunished?
translations.idiomatic: If recruitment brought rewards, flight surely demanded penalties.

sentences.zh: 今參詳修立賞罰十數條。”

translations.literal: Now after detailed review establish a dozen reward-and-punishment articles.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry now drafted more than ten articles of reward and punishment.

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: All approved.
translations.idiomatic: All granted.

sentences.zh: 五年，樞密院備童貫所言：“陝西等處差官招諭逃亡軍人，並許所在首身，更不會問，便支口券令歸本營。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the Bureau of Military Affairs prepared Tong Guan's statement: "Shaanxi and other places dispatched officials to summon and advise deserters; all were permitted to surrender wherever located, without further inquiry, and were immediately issued ration vouchers to return to original camps."
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 the bureau relayed Tong Guan's report that Shaanxi officials had been inviting deserters to surrender anywhere without interrogation and issuing travel rations for return to camp.

sentences.zh: 邊上軍人憚於戍守之勞，往往逃竄於內郡首身，遂得口券歸營，恐相習成風，有害軍政。

translations.literal: Frontier soldiers dread garrison labor, often flee to inner prefectures to surrender, then obtain vouchers and return to camp — feared this would become custom and harm military governance.
translations.idiomatic: Border troops, dreading garrison duty, were surrendering in interior prefectures to collect vouchers and return — a habit that would undermine discipline.

sentences.zh: 乞自今應軍人首身，並須會問逃亡赦限，依今來招諭指揮：若係赦後逃亡，即乞依條施行。”

translations.literal: I request that from now on all soldiers who surrender must be interrogated regarding desertion amnesty limits, according to current summoning orders: if desertion occurred after the amnesty, I request handling according to the articles.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that all surrenders be reviewed against amnesty deadlines, with post-amnesty deserters punished under the statutes.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 大觀三年，樞密院備臣僚言云：“自陝西路提點刑獄吳安憲始陳招誘逃亡廂禁軍之法，乃著許令投換改刺之令。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daguan, the Bureau prepared officials' statement: "Since Shaanxi circuit Judicial Intendant Wu Anxian first proposed methods to entice deserting provincial garrison troops, regulations permitting transfer and re-tattooing were established."
translations.idiomatic: In Daguan 3 officials traced the problem to Judicial Intendant Wu Anxian's policy of luring provincial garrison deserters with transfer and re-enlistment.

sentences.zh: 自此諸弊浸生，軍律不肅。

translations.literal: From this various abuses gradually arose, and military discipline was not strict.
translations.idiomatic: The practice had bred abuses and slackened discipline.

sentences.zh: 朝廷洞見其弊，已嚴立法，然尚有冒名一節，其弊未除。

translations.literal: The court saw through its abuses and had already strictly legislated, yet there remained the matter of false names — this abuse not yet removed.
translations.idiomatic: The court had tightened the law, yet fraud in enlistment remained.

sentences.zh: 請如主兵官舊曾占使書劄、作匠、雜技、手業之徒，或與統轄軍員素有嫌忌、意欲舍此而就彼，或所部逃亡數多，欲避譴責，輒將逃軍承逃亡之名便與請給。

translations.literal: I request regarding command officers who formerly held clerks, craftsmen, performers, and artisans, or who had old grievances with overseeing officers and wished to leave this for that, or whose units had many deserters and wished to avoid censure — rashly taking fugitives under desertion names and granting them pay.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders were filling rolls with fugitives under false names to cover deserters, avoid censure, or shift troublesome men or skilled laborers between units.

sentences.zh: 既避譴責，又冒請受，上下相蒙，莫之能革，致使軍士多懷擅去之心者，良以易得擅住之地也。

translations.literal: Having avoided censure, also falsely claimed pay — upper and lower deceived each other, none could reform it, causing many soldiers to harbor thoughts of leaving at will, truly because it was easy to find places to stay at will.
translations.idiomatic: Officers evaded blame while drawing fraudulent pay; fraud became entrenched, and soldiers learned they could desert with impunity.

sentences.zh: 若加重賞，申以嚴刑，庶革斯弊，有裨成法。”

translations.literal: If heavy rewards are added and strict punishment declared, perhaps this abuse can be reformed and benefit established law.
translations.idiomatic: He urged heavier rewards and stricter penalties to restore discipline.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 四年，樞密院言：“諸路及京畿逃亡軍數居多，雖赦敕立限許首，終懷畏避。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the bureau said: "All circuits and the capital region have many deserters; though amnesty edicts set limits permitting surrender, they still fear and avoid."
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 the bureau reported that deserters remained numerous despite amnesty deadlines.

sentences.zh: 若諸路專委知州、通判或職官一員，京畿委知縣，若招誘累及三百人以上，與減一年磨勘，五百人以上一年半，千人以上取旨推恩，於理為便。”

translations.literal: If each circuit specially entrusts a prefect, vice-prefect, or one official, and the capital entrusts county magistrates — if recruitment exceeds three hundred, reduce merit review one year; five hundred, one and a half years; one thousand, seek imperial grace — according to reason this is convenient.
translations.idiomatic: It proposed assigning local officials to recruit deserters, with merit-review reductions for three hundred or more men and imperial honors for one thousand or more.

sentences.zh: 政和二年，臣僚言：“祖宗軍政大備，無可議者。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenghe, officials said: "The forefathers' military governance was greatly complete; nothing to discuss."
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 2 officials declared that founding-era military institutions had been sound.

sentences.zh: 比多逃亡者，緣所在推行未至，及主兵司官遵奉未嚴故也。

translations.literal: Recently many deserters — because local implementation has not reached everywhere, and military command officials' compliance has not been strict.
translations.idiomatic: Recent desertions stemmed from lax enforcement by local and command officials.

sentences.zh: 其弊有六：一曰上下率斂，二曰舉放營債，三曰聚集賭博，四曰差使不均，五曰防送過遠，六曰單身無火聚。

translations.literal: Its abuses have six: first, extortion up and down; second, usurious camp loans; third, gambling gatherings; fourth, uneven assignments; fifth, escort duty too far; sixth, single men without household hearth.
translations.idiomatic: Six causes were cited: extortion, usurious camp loans, gambling, unfair assignments, excessive escort distances, and bachelor soldiers without family support.

sentences.zh: 似此雖具有條禁，而犯者極多。

translations.literal: Like these, though prohibitions exist, violators are extremely many.
translations.idiomatic: Though all were prohibited, violations were rampant.

sentences.zh: 欲乞下有司推究，除兵將官歲終立定賞罰條格外，詔諸路提刑司，每歲終將本路州軍不係將禁軍見管及逃亡人數，參互比較，具最多最少處各一州知、通職位姓名，申樞密院。”

translations.literal: I wish to request dispatch to relevant offices for investigation; besides commanders establishing year-end reward-and-punishment articles, edict circuit judicial commissions each year-end to compare provincial garrison current and desertion counts, report highest and lowest prefectures with magistrate names to the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: They asked for investigation, annual desertion comparisons by circuit judicial commissioners, and reports on best- and worst-performing prefectures.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 三年十一月，開封少尹陳彥修言：“諸廂收到寒凍赤露共五千七百餘人，其間逃軍數多，合行措置。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year, Kaifeng Vice Prefect Chen Yanxiu said: "All wards received five thousand seven hundred plus suffering cold exposure; among them many deserters — proper measures should be taken."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of year 3 Kaifeng Vice Prefect Chen Yanxiu reported more than 5,700 frostbite victims in the wards, many of them deserters requiring action.

sentences.zh: 今欲依押送逃軍格，每二十人各差使臣一員付與係押送人，各踏逐穩便官屋安泊，依居養法關請錢米存養，候晴和，管押前去。

translations.literal: Now I wish according to escort-deserter regulations, every twenty men to assign one envoy handed to escorts, each to seek stable official buildings to lodge, according to the relief law to request money and grain for care, wait for clear weather, and supervise escort forward.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed escorting them in parties of twenty to stable official shelters, providing relief rations under the residency-care law until fair weather allowed transit.

sentences.zh: 所有沿路支破口券，並依本府押送逃軍法，請於合破口券等外，更量支盤纏。”

translations.literal: All route travel vouchers according to the prefecture escort-deserter law; I request beyond proper vouchers additionally to allocate travel expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Travel vouchers were to follow standard deserter-escort rules, with additional travel funds beyond the usual allowances.

sentences.zh: 詔：“每人支盤纏錢三百，衲襖一領，候二月晴暖即行發遣。”

translations.literal: An edict: "Each person allocate travel money three hundred, one padded coat; wait until the second month is clear and warm, then dispatch."
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted each man three hundred cash, a padded jacket, and dispatch after fair weather in the second month.

sentences.zh: 四年，尚書省著令：“諸禁軍差發出戍未到軍前，或已到而代去半年以上，逃亡首獲，雖會恩，配如捕獲法；

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Ministry issued a regulation: "All forbidden army dispatched to garrison not yet reaching the army front, or arrived and relieved after half a year or more — desertion first captured, though meeting amnesty, assign per capture law;"
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 the ministry codified that deserters caught before reaching the front or after half a year of relief service were assigned per capture statutes even during amnesty.

sentences.zh: 上軍首身或捕獲，會恩，配依七日內法；

translations.literal: Upper army self-surrender or capture, meeting amnesty, assign per within-seven-days law;
translations.idiomatic: Upper-army deserters who surrendered or were captured during amnesty faced assignment under the seven-day rule.

sentences.zh: 下軍本名應配者，配千里。

translations.literal: Lower army original-name assignment — assign one thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Lower-army men liable for assignment were sent a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 若本管輒停留，與同罪，雖該赦仍依配法。”

translations.literal: If the original command rashly detains, same crime; though covered by amnesty still per assignment law.
translations.idiomatic: Units that illegally detained deserters shared the guilt, and assignment stood even under amnesty.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 五年，立錢監兵匠逃走刺手背法。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, established coin-mint artisan escape tattoo back-of-hand law.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 a law was enacted to tattoo the backs of mint workers' hands if they fled.

sentences.zh: 宣和二年，手詔：“逃卒頗多，仰宣撫司措置以聞。”

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuanhe, an imperial autograph: "Deserters are quite many — look to the Pacification Office to arrange and report."
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 2 an imperial note directed the Pacification Office to address rising desertions.

sentences.zh: 童貫言：“凡逃卒，冬祀大赦已有百日首身免罪之文，緣內有元犯雖首身，於常法尚合移降移配者，即未敢赴官自陳。

translations.literal: Tong Guan said: "All deserters — the winter sacrifice great amnesty already has hundred-day self-surrender pardon text; because among them original offenses, though surrendering, under normal law still warrant reduced sentence or reassigned exile — thus dare not go to office to declare."
translations.idiomatic: Tong Guan replied that winter amnesties allowed hundred-day surrenders, yet men with prior offenses feared reduced sentences or reassignment and would not come forward.

sentences.zh: 欲乞在京並京畿、京西、陝西、河東路逃軍，自今指揮到日，通未滿赦限共一百日，許令首身免罪，依舊軍分職次收管。

translations.literal: I wish to request capital, capital region, Jingxi, Shaanxi, and Hedong route deserters — from this order's arrival, totaling not yet full amnesty limit one hundred days, permit self-surrender pardon, according to original army branch and rank receive into custody.
translations.idiomatic: He asked a hundred-day surrender window for deserters in the capital region, Jingxi, Shaanxi, and Hedong, with restoration to original ranks.

sentences.zh: 仍免本司本營問儅，及放免官逋。

translations.literal: Still exempt original bureau and camp replacement liability, and release official debts.
translations.idiomatic: Replacement duties and official debts would be waived.

sentences.zh: 如本犯經冬祀赦後，猶有移降移配，特與原免。

translations.literal: If original offense after winter amnesty still has reduced sentence or reassignment — specially grant original pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Remaining penalties from pre-amnesty offenses would be specially waived.

sentences.zh: 若限滿不首，則依常法科罪。

translations.literal: If limit full and no surrender, then per normal law assign punishment.
translations.idiomatic: After the deadline, normal penalties would apply.

sentences.zh: 凡逃軍係在京住營，依限於在京首身者，令所隸軍司當日押赴本營。

translations.literal: All deserters registered in capital camps, surrendering within limit in the capital — order subordinate army bureau same day escort to original camp.
translations.idiomatic: Capital-based deserters surrendering in the capital were to be returned to camp the same day.

sentences.zh: 若見出戍者，即破口券轉押赴本路駐泊州軍，並依前項指揮免罪，依舊收管。

translations.literal: If currently on expedition, travel voucher transfer escort to home circuit garrison prefecture — all per prior order pardon, original custody.
translations.idiomatic: Men on expedition were to be escorted via travel voucher to their garrison circuit and restored to duty with amnesty.

sentences.zh: 凡逃軍在外，依限首身者，並於所在日破米二升，其縣、鎮、砦並限當日解本州軍，每二十人作一番，差職員管押，仍沿路給破口食，交付前路州軍，轉送住營去處。

translations.literal: All deserters outside, surrendering within limit — at location daily two sheng rice; counties, posts, and forts same day deliver to prefecture; every twenty a batch, assign official escort; route travel rations, hand to forward prefecture, transfer to camp location.
translations.idiomatic: Interior surrenders entitled men to two sheng of rice daily, same-day transfer in batches of twenty with escorts and travel rations to their home garrisons.

sentences.zh: 如見出戍，即轉駐泊州軍收管。

translations.literal: If currently on expedition, transfer to garrison prefecture custody.
translations.idiomatic: Expedition troops were held at their staging garrison.

sentences.zh: 凡首身軍人，並不許投換他軍。

translations.literal: All surrendering soldiers — not permitted to transfer to other armies.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendering soldiers could not transfer to other units.

sentences.zh: 凡所在當職官，如能於限內用心招收逃軍，措置轉送住營或出戍處收管，候滿，在外委提刑司，在京委開封府取索到營、出戍處公文，驗人數，最優者申宣撫司取旨推恩。”

translations.literal: All local responsible officials — if within limit diligently recruit deserters, arrange transfer to camp or expedition custody, after full — outside entrust judicial commission, capital entrust Kaifeng prefecture seek camp and expedition documents, verify numbers, best report to Pacification Office seek imperial grace.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who successfully returned deserters within the deadline could earn honors verified by the judicial commissioners or Kaifeng prefecture.

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: All approved.
translations.idiomatic: All granted.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔：“江、浙軍前等處應逃竄軍兵，並特放罪，許於本將見出軍路分州縣首身，依舊給請，隨處權行收管。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict: "Jiang and Zhe before army and such places fleeing soldiers — all specially grant pardon; permit at own general's current expedition route prefectures self-surrender, original pay, temporary custody wherever."
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 an edict pardoned deserters from Jiang-Zhe fronts, allowing surrender along expedition routes with restored pay and temporary local custody.

sentences.zh: 若走往他處，或於住營去處首獲，即令所在官司逐旋發遣赴本將應副使喚。

translations.literal: If flee elsewhere, or at camp location first captured — order local office successively dispatch to own general for service summons.
translations.idiomatic: Men captured elsewhere were to be sent promptly to their commander's summons.

sentences.zh: 仍委逐路安撫、鈐轄、提刑司覺察，如所在輒敢隱芘，或逐司不行覺察，並論違製。”

translations.literal: Still entrust each route Pacification, Command, and Judicial commissions to inspect; if anywhere dare conceal or commissions fail to inspect — all judged violation of regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification, command, and judicial officers were charged with oversight; concealment would be punished as a regulatory violation.

sentences.zh: 四年，臣僚言：“中外士卒無故逃亡，所在有之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, officials said: "Central and external soldiers without cause desert — everywhere there are such."
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 officials reported that desertion without cause was widespread throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 祖宗治軍紀律甚嚴，若在戍者還家，當役者避事，必有轅門之戮。

translations.literal: The founding emperors governed the army with very strict discipline; if those on garrison duty returned home or those on active service shirked their duties, execution at the camp gate was inevitable.
translations.idiomatic: Under the founding emperors, military discipline was severe: garrison soldiers who went home or active-duty men who shirked service faced execution at the camp gate.

sentences.zh: 今既宥其罪，且許投換，不製於什伍之長；

translations.literal: Now their crimes are already pardoned, and they are permitted to transfer and reassignment, not constrained by squad leaders;
translations.idiomatic: Today they are pardoned and allowed to transfer to other units without permission from squad leaders;

sentences.zh: 既立赦限，又特展日，以寬其自首之期。

translations.literal: Amnesty deadlines have been set, and days have been specially extended to broaden the period for voluntary surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty deadlines were set—and then extended—to give deserters more time to turn themselves in.

sentences.zh: 臣恐逃亡得計，其弊益滋。

translations.literal: Your subject fears deserters will get their way, and the abuse will grow worse.
translations.idiomatic: I fear deserters will take advantage of this, and the problem will only grow worse.

sentences.zh: 乞除恩赦外不輕與限，使知限之不可為常，庶有畏懼。”

translations.literal: I beg that aside from general amnesties, grace periods not be granted lightly, so they know limits cannot become routine, and perhaps they will have fear."
translations.idiomatic: Aside from general amnesties, please do not grant grace periods casually, so soldiers learn that leniency is not permanent and retain some fear of punishment.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 五年，臣僚言：“今諸軍逃亡者不以實聞。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, officials said: "Today deserters from the various armies are not reported truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 officials reported that deserters from the various armies were not being reported truthfully.

sentences.zh: 諸處冒名請給，至於揀閱差役，則巧為占破，甚不獲已，則雇募逋逃以充名數，旋即遁去，無復實用。

translations.literal: Everywhere people fraudulently claim names and draw rations; when it comes to muster and assignment of duty, they cleverly fill quotas; when utterly unable to do so, they hire fugitive deserters to fill the rolls, who immediately flee again, of no real use.
translations.idiomatic: Units everywhere drew pay under false names; at muster they padded the rolls, and when they could not, they hired fugitive deserters to fill quotas—who promptly fled again—leaving no one of real use.

sentences.zh: 平居難於供億，緩急無以應用。

translations.literal: In normal times it is hard to sustain payments; in emergencies there is no one to deploy.
translations.idiomatic: In peacetime the burden of pay was hard to sustain; in crisis there was no one to deploy.

sentences.zh: 而奸人攘臂其間，坐費財賦。

translations.literal: Meanwhile rascals insert themselves among them and simply waste state revenues.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile schemers inserted themselves and simply wasted state revenues.

sentences.zh: 雖開收勘斂，法製滋詳，而共利之人，一體傅會。

translations.literal: Although collection and verification were opened, and regulations grew ever more detailed, those who shared in the profit all collaborated in subterfuge.
translations.idiomatic: Though collection and verification procedures were introduced and regulations grew ever more detailed, those who profited from the fraud all colluded.

sentences.zh: 望賜處分，先令當職官核見實數，保明申達轉運司，期日委諸郡守貳點閱，仍關掌兵官司照會行下；

translations.literal: We hope for disposal: first have responsible officials verify actual numbers, certify and report to the Transport Commission; on fixed dates commission prefectural deputies to inspect, and notify military offices to carry this out;
translations.idiomatic: We ask that responsible officials first verify actual head counts, certify them to the Transport Commission, and on fixed dates have prefectural deputies inspect the rolls, with military offices notified to enforce the order;

sentences.zh: 不可勾押至州者，差官就閱，期以同日究見的實。

translations.literal: Those who cannot be summoned to the prefecture—dispatch officials to inspect on site, with the same deadline to determine the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Where soldiers could not be summoned to the prefectural seat, officials should inspect on site, with the same deadline to establish the truth.

sentences.zh: 稍涉欺罔，根治不赦。

translations.literal: Any involvement in fraud—thoroughly investigate and no pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Any fraud should be thoroughly investigated and punished without pardon.

sentences.zh: 監司使者分郡覆實，具數申達於朝，以待差官分按，必行罪賞，使官無虛費，而軍有實用，則紀律可明，國用可省。”

translations.literal: Supervisory commissioners should verify by prefecture, report numbers to court, await dispatched inspectors to investigate by region, necessarily apply punishment and reward, so offices have no wasted expenditure and armies have real effect—then discipline can be clarified and state revenues saved."
translations.idiomatic: Supervisory commissioners should verify by prefecture and report to court; dispatched inspectors should investigate by region and enforce rewards and punishments, so offices waste no funds, armies have real strength, discipline is restored, and state revenues are saved.

sentences.zh: 詔送樞密院條畫措置。

translations.literal: An edict ordered it sent to the Bureau of Military Affairs to draft measures.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the proposal sent to the Bureau of Military Affairs to draft implementing measures.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，尚書省言：“開封府狀：‘乞應在京犯盜配降出外之人，復走入京投換者，許人告捕，科以逃亡捕獲之罪，酌情增配。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, second month, the Ministry said: "Kaifeng Prefecture reports: 'Request that those who committed theft in the capital, were assigned to exile outside, and then re-entered the capital to transfer and reassignment—permit people to inform and capture them, punish under the law for captured deserters, and appropriately increase their assignment.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, month 2, the ministry reported that Kaifeng Prefecture requested: those convicted of theft in the capital, exiled outside, and who then re-entered the capital to enlist elsewhere should be subject to informant capture, punished under deserter-capture statutes, and given an increased assignment.

sentences.zh: 其官司及本營典首人員、曹級容庇收留，各杖一百；

translations.literal: Officials and unit clerks who shelter them—each one hundred strokes of the cane;
translations.idiomatic: Officials and unit clerks who sheltered them would each receive one hundred strokes of the cane;

sentences.zh: 因致為盜者，依差使配軍入京作過法，與犯人同罪。

translations.literal: Those who thereby become robbers—under the law for dispatched soldiers assigned to the capital who commit crimes, same guilt as the offender.
translations.idiomatic: Those who thereby turned to robbery would be punished under the statute for dispatched soldiers who commit crimes in the capital, with the same guilt as the offender.

sentences.zh: 罪止徒二年，不以去官赦原減。

translations.literal: Maximum punishment is two years penal servitude, not reducible by amnesty upon leaving office.
translations.idiomatic: The maximum penalty was two years penal servitude, not reducible by amnesty upon leaving office.

sentences.zh: 及在京犯罪編管出外逃亡入京之人，雖有斷罪增加地裏條法，緣止是募告賞格太輕，是致往往復走入京。

translations.literal: And those who committed crimes in the capital, were placed under guarded exile outside, and fled back to the capital—although there are laws for increased assignment by region upon conviction, the reward for informants is too light, which causes many to repeatedly re-enter the capital.
translations.idiomatic: As for those convicted in the capital, placed under guarded exile outside, and who fled back to the capital—though statutes provided for increased assignment by region, rewards for informants were too light, and many repeatedly returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 欲乞元犯杖罪賞錢十貫，徒罪二十貫，流罪三十貫，並以犯事人家財充。

translations.literal: Request that original offenders of cane punishment—reward ten strings of cash; penal servitude—twenty strings; exile—thirty strings—all from the offender's family property.
translations.idiomatic: They requested rewards of ten strings of cash for original cane offenses, twenty for penal servitude, and thirty for exile—all drawn from the offender's family property.

sentences.zh: ’”從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔：“應諸路逃竄軍人或已該赦恩出首避免，卻歸出戍去處再行逃竄之人，令於所在去處首身，並特與免罪，於一般軍分安排，支破請給，發赴軍前使喚。”

translations.literal: Twelfth month, edict: "All circuit deserters, or those who benefited from amnesty by turning themselves in to avoid punishment but returned to their garrison posts and deserted again—order them to surrender wherever they are, specially grant amnesty, assign them to regular units, pay their rations, and dispatch them to the front for service.
translations.idiomatic: In month 12 an edict ordered that deserters from all circuits—including those who had surrendered under amnesty but then returned to their garrison posts and deserted again—must surrender wherever they were found, would be specially pardoned, assigned to regular units, paid their rations, and dispatched to the front for service.

sentences.zh: 六月，詔：“應河東潰散諸路將佐，並仰逐路帥守發遣赴河東、河北製置司，以功贖過。”

translations.literal: Sixth month, edict: "All dispersed officers from various circuits in Hedong—all circuit commanders should dispatch them to the Hedong and Hebei Preparation Commissions to redeem their faults through merit."
translations.idiomatic: In month 6 an edict ordered that dispersed officers from all circuits in Hedong be dispatched by their circuit commanders to the Hedong and Hebei preparation commissions to redeem their faults through merit.

sentences.zh: 河北路製置司都統製王淵言：“被旨差充招集種師道等下潰散人馬，應援太原，限滿不首，即寄禁家屬，許人收捕赴軍前，重行處置。”

translations.literal: Hebei Preparation Commission supreme commander Wang Yuan said: "By imperial order appointed to gather dispersed troops under Zhong Shidao and others, to reinforce Taiyuan—if deadline passes without surrender, detain their families, permit people to capture and deliver them to the army front for severe punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Hebei preparation commission supreme commander Wang Yuan reported: by imperial order he had been appointed to gather the dispersed troops under Zhong Shidao and others to reinforce Taiyuan; those who failed to surrender by the deadline would have their families detained, and informants were permitted to capture them and deliver them to the front for severe punishment.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 仍自指揮到日，限以十日。

translations.literal: Furthermore from the day the order arrives, limit to ten days.
translations.idiomatic: The deadline was set at ten days from the day the order arrived.

sentences.zh: 河北路製使劉韐奏：“近製置使種師中領軍到於榆次，失利潰散，師中不知存在。

translations.literal: Hebei commissioner Liu Ge memorialized: "Recently preparation commissioner Zhong Shizhong led troops to Yuci, suffered defeat and dispersion, and Shizhong's whereabouts are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei commissioner Liu Ge memorialized: recently preparation commissioner Zhong Shizhong had led troops to Yuci, suffered defeat and rout, and Shizhong's fate was unknown.

sentences.zh: 奉旨，師中下應統製、將佐、使臣等，並與放罪。

translations.literal: By imperial order, all commanders, officers, and envoys under Shizhong were granted amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order, all commanders, officers, and envoys under Shizhong had been granted amnesty.

sentences.zh: 臣按：用兵失主將，統製、將佐並合行軍法。

translations.literal: Your subject observes: in warfare, when the commanding general is lost, commanders and officers should all be subject to military law.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject observes that when an army loses its commanding general in battle, commanders and officers should all be subject to military law.

sentences.zh: 軍法行，則人以主將為重，緩急必須護救。

translations.literal: When military law is enforced, men regard the commanding general as paramount, and in crisis they must protect and rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: When military law is enforced, men regard the commanding general as paramount and in crisis must protect and rescue him.

sentences.zh: 若不行軍法，緩急之際爭先逃遁，視主將如路人，略不顧恤。

translations.literal: If military law is not enforced, in crisis all scramble to flee first, treating the commanding general like a stranger, utterly without concern.
translations.idiomatic: If military law is not enforced, in crisis all scramble to flee first, treating the commanding general like a stranger and showing no concern at all.

sentences.zh: 近年以來，高永年陷歿，一行將佐及中軍將、提轄等未嚐罪以軍法，繼而劉法陷歿，今種師中又死王事。

translations.literal: In recent years when Gao Yongnian fell in battle, the officers and central army commanders were never punished under military law; then Liu Fa fell; now Zhong Shizhong has died in service of the state.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years when Gao Yongnian fell in battle, his officers and central army commanders were never punished under military law; then Liu Fa fell; now Zhong Shizhong has died in the service of the state.

sentences.zh: 若兩軍相遇，勢力不加，血戰而敗，或失主將，亦無可言。

translations.literal: If two armies meet and strength is insufficient, fighting to the bloody end and losing, or losing the commander—nothing more need be said.
translations.idiomatic: If two armies meet when strength is insufficient, and men fight to the bloody end and lose, or lose their commander—nothing more need be said.

sentences.zh: 榆次之戰，頃刻而潰，統製、將佐、使臣走者十已八九，軍士中傷十無一二，獨師中不出。

translations.literal: At the Battle of Yuci, rout came in moments—eight or nine out of ten commanders and officers fled; among soldiers, wounded were scarcely one or two in ten; only Shizhong did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: At the Battle of Yuci the army broke in moments: eight or nine out of ten commanders and officers fled, scarcely one or two soldiers in ten were wounded, and only Shizhong did not escape.

sentences.zh: 若謂師中撫禦少恩，紀律不嚴，而其受命即行，奮不顧身，初聞右軍戰卻，即遣應援，比時諸將已無在者。

translations.literal: Even if one says Shizhong was insufficiently gracious in command and discipline was lax, he accepted his commission and marched at once, reckless of his life; hearing the right wing had broken, he immediately sent reinforcements—but by then none of the officers remained.
translations.idiomatic: Even if one holds that Shizhong was insufficiently gracious in command and discipline was lax, he accepted his commission and marched at once, reckless of his life; hearing the right wing had broken, he immediately sent reinforcements—but by then none of the other officers remained.

sentences.zh: 至賊兵犯營，師中猶未肯上馬。

translations.literal: When enemy troops attacked the camp, Shizhong still refused to mount his horse.
translations.idiomatic: When enemy troops attacked the camp, Shizhong still refused to mount his horse and flee.

sentences.zh: 使師中有偷生之心，聞敗即行，亦必得出。

translations.literal: Had Shizhong harbored any wish to save his own life, he would surely have gotten out the moment he heard of defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Had Shizhong harbored any wish to save his own life, he would surely have escaped the moment he heard of defeat.

sentences.zh: 一時將佐若能戮力相救，或可破敵。

translations.literal: If the officers at that moment had united their strength to rescue him, they might have broken the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: If the officers at that moment had united to rescue him, they might have broken the enemy.

sentences.zh: 今一軍才卻，諸將不有主帥，相繼而遁。

translations.literal: Now as soon as one army wavers, the officers, disregarding their commander, flee one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Now as soon as one wing wavers, the officers, disregarding their commander, flee one after another.

sentences.zh: 其初猶有懼色，既聞放罪，遂皆釋然。

translations.literal: At first they still showed fear; once they heard of amnesty, they all relaxed entirely.
translations.idiomatic: At first they still showed fear; once they heard of amnesty, they all relaxed entirely.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以太原之圍未解，未欲窮治。

translations.literal: The court, because Taiyuan's siege was not yet lifted, did not wish to pursue the matter to the end.
translations.idiomatic: The court, because the siege of Taiyuan was not yet lifted, did not wish to pursue the matter to the end.

sentences.zh: 今師旅方興，深恐無所懲艾，遇敵必不用命。

translations.literal: Now armies are being raised anew; I deeply fear there will be no deterrent, and when meeting the enemy they will surely not give their all.
translations.idiomatic: Now armies are being raised anew; I deeply fear there will be no deterrent, and when they meet the enemy they will surely not give their all.

sentences.zh: 欲乞指揮，應種師中下統製、將佐並依聖旨處分，仍令軍前自效。

translations.literal: Request an order that all commanders and officers under Shizhong be dealt with according to the imperial will, yet still sent to the front to prove themselves.
translations.idiomatic: I request an order that all commanders and officers under Shizhong be dealt with according to the imperial will, yet still sent to the front to prove themselves.

sentences.zh: 如能用命立功。

translations.literal: If they obey orders and achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: If they obey orders and achieve merit,

sentences.zh: 與免前罪；

translations.literal: Their previous guilt shall be pardoned;
translations.idiomatic: their previous guilt shall be pardoned;

sentences.zh: 今後非立戰功，雖該恩赦不得敘復。

translations.literal: Henceforth, unless they establish battlefield merit, even if covered by amnesty they may not be restored to rank.
translations.idiomatic: henceforth, unless they establish battlefield merit, even if covered by amnesty they may not be restored to rank.

sentences.zh: 仍乞優詔褒贈師中，以為忠義之勸。”

translations.literal: Also request an exceptional edict to posthumously honor Shizhong as encouragement to loyalty and righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: I also request an exceptional edict to posthumously honor Shizhong as encouragement to loyalty and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 詔：“種師中下統製、將佐並降五官，仍開具職位、姓名申尚書省，餘依劉韐所奏。”

translations.literal: Edict: "All commanders and officers under Shizhong demoted five ranks; submit a list of positions and names to the Ministry; remainder per Liu Ge's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that all commanders and officers under Shizhong be demoted five ranks, that a list of positions and names be submitted to the ministry, and that the remainder follow Liu Ge's memorial.

sentences.zh: 八月，河北、河東路宣撫司奏：“近據都統製王淵捉獲潰敗使臣，已管押赴宣撫副使劉韐軍前交割，依軍法施行外，訪聞尚有未曾出首將佐、使臣。”

translations.literal: Eighth month, Hebei and Hedong Pacification Commission reported: "Recently supreme commander Wang Yuan captured dispersed envoys and delivered them to deputy commissioner Liu Ge's army for military law execution; we have heard there are still officers and envoys who have not surrendered."
translations.idiomatic: In month 8 the Hebei and Hedong pacification commission reported that supreme commander Wang Yuan had captured dispersed envoys and delivered them to deputy commissioner Liu Ge's army for execution under military law, but that officers and envoys who had not yet surrendered were still at large.

sentences.zh: 詔：“限今指揮到日更與展限十日，許令於所在州軍出首，仍依元降指揮免罪，特與支破遞馬驛券，疾速發赴軍前自效，候立功日優加推賞。

translations.literal: Edict: "From the day this order arrives extend ten more days; permit them to surrender at their local garrison; still grant amnesty per the original order; specially provide courier vouchers; speedily dispatch to the front to prove themselves; upon merit grant exceptional rewards.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that from the day it arrived ten more days be granted; they were permitted to surrender at their local garrison, would still be pardoned under the original order, would receive courier vouchers, and would be speedily dispatched to the front to prove themselves, with exceptional rewards upon merit.

sentences.zh: 如再限滿日更不首身，當取見職名重賞購捕，定行軍法。

translations.literal: If after the extended deadline they still do not surrender, publish names and offer heavy rewards for capture; military law will be enforced without exception.
translations.idiomatic: If after the extended deadline they still did not surrender, their names would be published and heavy rewards offered for capture, and military law would be enforced without exception.

sentences.zh: 仍多出榜示諭。”

translations.literal: Also post many notices to publicize this.
translations.idiomatic: Many notices were also to be posted to publicize the order.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，詔：“訪聞諸處潰散軍人嘯聚作過，將百姓強刺充軍，驅虜隨行使喚，遇敵使前，害枉良民。

translations.literal: Second year, fourth month, edict: "We have learned that dispersed soldiers gathering in bands commit outrages, forcibly tattoo civilians as soldiers, drive captives as attendants, send them ahead to meet the enemy, harming innocent people.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, month 4, an edict reported that dispersed soldiers gathering in bands were committing outrages, forcibly tattooing civilians as soldiers, driving captives as attendants, sending them ahead to meet the enemy, and harming innocent people.

sentences.zh: 其令有司榜諭：被虜強刺之人許以自陳，給據各令歸業。

translations.literal: Order authorities to post notices: those forcibly tattooed while captured may declare themselves and receive certificates to return to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Authorities were ordered to post notices: those forcibly tattooed while captured might declare themselves and receive certificates to return to their occupations.

sentences.zh: 願充軍者，隨等杖刺填禁、廂軍，依條支給例物。”

translations.literal: Those willing to serve may be tattooed by rank and fill the Forbidden or Garrison Armies, with standard provisions per regulations."
translations.idiomatic: Those willing to serve would be tattooed by rank and assigned to the forbidden or garrison armies, with standard provisions per regulations.

sentences.zh: 又詔：“昨逃亡班直、諸軍，雖已降指揮撫諭，並與免罪，發歸元處。

translations.literal: Another edict: "Yesterday's deserters among the palace guards and various armies—though orders were already issued offering amnesty and sending them back to their original posts.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict addressed deserters among the palace guards and various armies: though orders had already been issued offering amnesty and sending them back to their original posts,

sentences.zh: 其管押兵官未有指揮，可候指揮到，許於所在官司自陳，亦與免罪。”

translations.literal: Escort officers without orders—when the order arrives, permit them to declare at local offices, also granted amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: escort officers who had not yet received orders might, once the order arrived, declare themselves at local offices and also be granted amnesty.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，招募多西北之人，其後令諸路州、軍、砦或三衙招募，或選刺三衙軍中子弟，或從諸郡選刺中軍子弟解發。

translations.literal: At the start of Jianyan, recruitment drew mainly northwesterners; afterward circuits' prefectures, garrisons, and fortresses, or the Three Commands, were to recruit; or select sons of Three Commands soldiers for tattooing; or select sons of central army soldiers from various prefectures and dispatch them.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianyan era recruitment drew mainly on northwesterners; afterward circuits' prefectures, garrisons, and fortresses, or the Three Commands, were to recruit, or select sons of Three Commands soldiers for tattooing, or select sons of central army soldiers from various prefectures and dispatch them.

sentences.zh: 復詔滄、濱及江、淮沿流州軍，募善沒水經時伏藏者，以五千為額。

translations.literal: Another edict: prefectures along Cangzhou, Binzhou, and the Yangtze-Huai waterways recruit skilled divers who can hold breath underwater for extended periods, quota of five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict ordered prefectures along Cangzhou, Binzhou, and the Yangtze-Huai waterways to recruit skilled divers who could hold their breath underwater for extended periods, with a quota of five thousand.

sentences.zh: 神武右軍統製張俊言：“牙軍多招集烏合之眾，擬上等改刺勝捷，次等刺振華、振武，庶得部分歸一訓練為便。”

translations.literal: Shenwu Right Army commander Zhang Jun said: "The guard corps has gathered many rabble; propose reassigning superior men to Shengjie, second rank to Zhenhua and Zhenwu, so sections can be unified for training."
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu Right Army commander Zhang Jun reported that the guard corps had gathered much rabble and proposed reassigning superior men to Shengjie and second-rank men to Zhenhua and Zhenwu so that units could be unified for training.

sentences.zh: 詔兩浙、江東，除江陰軍，各募水軍二百人。

translations.literal: Edict: Two Zhe and Jiangdong, except Jiangyin Army, each recruit two hundred naval troops.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Two Zhe and Jiangdong, except Jiangyin Army, each to recruit two hundred naval troops.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，廣東帥臣言：“本路將兵元五千二百，見千三百十九。

translations.literal: Shaoxing first year, Guangdong commander said: "This circuit's garrison troops originally five thousand two hundred, currently one thousand three hundred nineteen.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoxing the Guangdong commander reported that the circuit's garrison troops had originally numbered 5,200 but now stood at 1,319.

sentences.zh: 今擬將官駐紮諸軍洎本路州軍，以十分為率，各招其半。”

translations.literal: Now propose stationed officers and circuit prefecture garrisons each recruit half their quota on a ten-part basis.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that stationed officers and circuit prefecture garrisons each recruit half their quota on a ten-part basis.

sentences.zh: 二年，累降令行在諸軍，毋互相招收，及將別軍人拘執，違者行軍法。

translations.literal: Second year, repeated edicts to capital garrisons: do not recruit from each other or detain other units' soldiers—violators face military law.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 repeated edicts to the capital garrisons forbade recruiting from each other or detaining soldiers from other units; violators would face military law.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔：“所招河北人充河北振武，餘人刺陝西振華指揮。

translations.literal: Fourth year, edict: "Recruited Hebei men fill Hebei Zhenwu units; others tattooed into Shaanxi Zhenhua commands.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 an edict ordered that recruited Hebei men fill Hebei Zhenwu units and that others be tattooed into Shaanxi Zhenhua commands.

sentences.zh: 沿江招置水軍，備戰艦，募東南諳水者充，每指揮以五百為額。”

translations.literal: Along the Yangtze establish naval forces with warships; recruit southeastern men skilled in water; each command quota five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Along the Yangtze naval forces were to be established with warships; southeastern men skilled in water were to be recruited, with a quota of five hundred per command.

sentences.zh: 十年，詔三京路招撫處置使司招效用軍兵萬人，內招使臣二千員。

translations.literal: Tenth year, edict: Three Capitals Pacification Commission recruit ten thousand utility troops, including two thousand officer-envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 an edict ordered the Three Capitals pacification commission to recruit ten thousand utility troops, including two thousand officer-envoys.

sentences.zh: 十五年，福建安撫莫將言：“汀、漳、泉、建四州，與廣東、江西接壤。

translations.literal: Fifteenth year, Fujian pacification commissioner Mo Jiang said: "The four prefectures Ding, Zhang, Quan, and Jian border Guangdong and Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 Fujian pacification commissioner Mo Jiang reported that the four prefectures of Ding, Zhang, Quan, and Jian bordered Guangdong and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 比年寇盜剽劫居民，土豪備私錢集社戶，防捍有勞，有司不為上聞推恩，破家無所依歸，勢必從賊。

translations.literal: In recent years bandits plunder residents; local strongmen spend private funds gathering community households for defense; officials fail to report their merit—bankrupt with nowhere to turn, they inevitably join the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years bandits had plundered residents; local strongmen spent private funds gathering community households for defense, but officials failed to report their merit; ruined and with nowhere to turn, they inevitably joined the bandits.

sentences.zh: 官軍不習山險，且瘴癘侵加，不能窮追，管屬良民悉轉為盜。

translations.literal: Government troops are unused to mountain terrain and suffer malarial pestilence; unable to pursue to the end, all governed civilians become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops were unused to mountain terrain and suffered malarial pestilence; unable to pursue to the end, all the civilians under their jurisdiction turned to banditry.

sentences.zh: 請委四州守臣，募此遊手無歸勇健之人，各收千人，仍以效用為名，足可備用，實永久利。”

translations.literal: Request commissioning the four prefectures to recruit rootless strongmen, one thousand each, under the name of utility troops—sufficient for preparedness, a lasting benefit."
translations.idiomatic: He requested that the four prefectures recruit rootless strongmen, one thousand each, under the name of utility troops—enough for preparedness and a lasting benefit.

sentences.zh: 詔令張淵同措置。

translations.literal: Edict ordered Zhang Yuan to handle it jointly.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Zhang Yuan to handle the matter jointly.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，殿前都指揮使楊存中言：“舊制，在京所管捧日、天武、拱聖、驍騎、驍勝、寧朔、神騎、神勇、宣武、虎翼、廣勇諸指揮禁軍內，捧日、天武依條升揀扈衛諸班直，拱聖、神勇以下升揀捧日、天武，除逃亡有故，僅千九百人。

translations.literal: Twenty-fourth year, Palace Front commander Yang Cunzhong said: "Under the old system, among the capital's Pengri, Tianwu, Gongsheng, Xiaoqi, Xiaosheng, Ningshuo, Shenqi, Shenyong, Xuanwu, Huyi, Guangyong forbidden armies—in Pengri and Tianwu select for palace guard duty; from Gongsheng and Shenyong downward select for Pengri and Tianwu—excluding deserters with excuse, barely one thousand nine hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24 Palace Front commander Yang Cunzhong reported that under the old system, among the capital's Pengri, Tianwu, Gongsheng, Xiaoqi, Xiaosheng, Ningshuo, Shenqi, Shenyong, Xuanwu, Huyi, and Guangyong forbidden armies, Pengri and Tianwu selected men for palace guard duty and Gongsheng, Shenyong, and lower units selected men for Pengri and Tianwu; excluding deserters with valid excuse, barely 1,900 remained.

sentences.zh: 請於今年分定月內招千人。”

translations.literal: Request recruiting one thousand within the designated months this year.
translations.idiomatic: He requested recruiting one thousand within the designated months of that year.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，楊存中奉旨，三衙所招效用兵令住招。

translations.literal: Twenty-seventh year, Yang Cunzhong received order that Three Commands utility recruitment should halt.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 Yang Cunzhong received an order that the Three Commands' utility recruitment should halt.

sentences.zh: 今闕六千七百二十六人，若不招填，兵數日損。

translations.literal: Now short six thousand seven hundred twenty-six; if not recruited to fill, troop numbers daily decline.
translations.idiomatic: The shortfall now stood at 6,726; if not recruited to fill, troop numbers would daily decline.

sentences.zh: 詔本司來年正月為始，依舊招募。

translations.literal: Edict: this bureau from next year's first month resume recruitment as before.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered this bureau to resume recruitment as before starting the first month of the following year.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年，步軍司郭振言：“本司在京日軍額三萬九千五百，今行在僅千二百一十九。”

translations.literal: In Longxing 1, Guo Zhen of the Infantry Office said: "When this office was in the capital, its troop quota was 39,500; now at the temporary capital it is only 1,219."
translations.idiomatic: In Longxing 1, Guo Zhen of the Infantry Office reported, "When this office was in the capital, its troop quota was 39,500; now at the temporary capital it is only 1,219."

sentences.zh: 詔招填千七百八十一人，以三千為額，刺充神衛，虎翼，飛山、床子弩雄武等指揮。

translations.literal: An edict ordered recruiting 1,781 men to fill the ranks, making 3,000 the quota, and tattooing them to fill such commands as Shenwei, Huyi, Feishan, Chuangzi Crossbow, and Xiongwu.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered 1,781 men recruited to bring the quota to 3,000 and tattooed into the Shenwei, Huyi, Feishan, Chuangzi Crossbow, Xiongwu, and other commands.

sentences.zh: 乾道七年，馬軍司王友直言：“見管戰馬二千七百餘，止有傔馬六百餘人，請招傔兵千五百，並充雄威。”

translations.literal: Qiandao seventh year, Cavalry Bureau Wang Youzhi said: "Currently two thousand seven hundred plus war horses, only six hundred plus grooms—request recruiting one thousand five hundred grooms, all assigned to Xiongwei."
translations.idiomatic: In Qiandao year 7 Cavalry Bureau director Wang Youzhi reported that the bureau had more than 2,700 war horses but only 600-odd grooms, and requested recruiting 1,500 grooms, all assigned to Xiongwei.

sentences.zh: 詔招千人，刺“步傔”二字。

translations.literal: Edict: recruit one thousand, tattoo the two characters "foot groom."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered recruiting one thousand men, tattooed with the characters for foot groom.

sentences.zh: 步軍司吳挺言：“步司五軍，額二萬五千，見闕三千六百。”

translations.literal: Infantry Bureau Wu Ting said: "Five infantry armies, quota twenty-five thousand, currently short three thousand six hundred."
translations.idiomatic: Infantry Bureau director Wu Ting reported that the five infantry armies had a quota of 25,000 but were currently short 3,600.

sentences.zh: 詔令招填。

translations.literal: Edict ordered recruitment to fill quota.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered recruitment to fill the quota.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十六年，殿前副都指揮郭鈞言：“淳熙五年住招兵，今逾十載，戰隊合用火分傔兵闕。”

translations.literal: Chunxi sixteenth year, deputy Palace Front commander Guo Jun said: "Recruitment halted in Chunxi fifth year; now over ten years—fire-team grooms for combat units are short."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chunxi6 deputy Palace Front commander Guo Jun reported that recruitment had halted in Chunxi year 5; now more than ten years had passed, and fire-team grooms for combat units were short.

sentences.zh: 詔招千人。

translations.literal: Edict: recruit one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered recruiting one thousand.

sentences.zh: 紹熙二年，詔步軍司招軍千人。

translations.literal: Shaoxi second year, edict: Infantry Bureau recruit one thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxi year 2 an edict ordered the Infantry Bureau to recruit one thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 寶慶二年，知武岡軍吳愈言：“禁衛兵所以重根本、威外夷，太祖聚天下精兵在京者十餘萬，州郡亦十餘萬。

translations.literal: Baoqing second year, Wugang prefect Wu Yu said: "Palace guard troops strengthen the root and awe foreigners—Taizu gathered over one hundred thousand elite troops in the capital, prefectures also over one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoqing year 2 Wugang prefect Wu Yu reported that palace guard troops strengthened the root and awed foreigners: Taizu had gathered more than 100,000 elite troops in the capital, and prefectures also held more than 100,000.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十五年，三衛馬步諸軍凡七萬餘，闕舊額三萬，若以川蜀、荊襄、兩淮屯戍較之，奚啻數倍於禁衛？

translations.literal: Jiading fifteenth year, Three Commands horse and foot total over seventy thousand, short thirty thousand of original quota—compared with garrisons in Sichuan, Jing-Xiang, and Huai regions, are they not several times the palace guard?
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiading5 the Three Commands' horse and foot armies totaled over 70,000, short 30,000 of the original quota—compared with garrisons in Sichuan, Jing-Xiang, and the two Huai regions, were they not several times the palace guard?

sentences.zh: 宜遵舊制，擇州郡禁兵補禁衛闕，州郡闕額帥守招填。”

translations.literal: Should follow old system: select prefecture forbidden troops to fill palace guard shortfalls; prefecture shortfalls filled by commanders.
translations.idiomatic: The old system should be followed: select prefecture forbidden troops to fill palace guard shortfalls, and have commanders recruit to fill prefecture shortfalls.

sentences.zh: 紹定四年，臣僚言：“州郡有禁卒，有壯城，有廂軍，有土兵，一州之財自足以給一州之兵。

translations.literal: Shaoding fourth year, officials said: "Prefectures have forbidden troops, city guards, garrison armies, local militia—one prefecture's finances should suffice for one prefecture's troops.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoding year 4 officials reported that prefectures had forbidden troops, city guards, garrison armies, and local militia, and that one prefecture's finances should suffice for one prefecture's troops.

sentences.zh: 比年尺籍多虛，月招歲補，悉成文具。

translations.literal: In recent years rosters are largely fictitious; monthly recruitment and annual filling all become empty formality.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years rosters were largely fictitious; monthly recruitment and annual filling had all become empty formality.

sentences.zh: 蓋州郡吝養兵之費，所招無二三，逃亡已六七。

translations.literal: Because prefectures begrudge troop maintenance costs, of those recruited barely two or three remain, while six or seven have deserted.
translations.idiomatic: Because prefectures begrudged the cost of maintaining troops, of those recruited barely two or three remained, while six or seven had already deserted.

sentences.zh: 宜申嚴帥臣，應郡守到罷，具兵額若干、逃故若干、招填若干、考其數而黜陟之。”

translations.literal: It is fitting to warn circuit commanders strictly: when prefects arrive or depart, they should report how many troops were authorized, how many deserted or died, and how many were recruited to fill gaps, and promotions and demotions should follow review of those figures.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit commanders should be ordered that every incoming or outgoing prefect must report authorized strength, desertions and deaths, and recruitment totals, with promotion and demotion tied to those numbers.

sentences.zh: 寶祐間，州郡闕守，承攝者遣令招刺，不詢材武，務盜帑儲。

translations.literal: During the Baoyou period, when prefectures lacked regular prefects, acting officials sent orders to recruit and tattoo without asking about talent or martial skill, striving only to plunder treasury stores.
translations.idiomatic: In the Baoyou era, vacant prefectures were run by acting officials who ordered recruitment without testing ability, chiefly to loot public funds.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳季年，邊報日聞，召募尤急，官降錢甚優厚。

translations.literal: In the closing years of Xianchun, frontier reports came daily, recruitment was especially urgent, and official bounty money was very generous.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Xianchun years, daily frontier alarms made recruitment desperate and court bounties unusually rich.

sentences.zh: 強刺平民，非無法禁。

translations.literal: Forcibly tattooing commoners was not without laws forbidding it.
translations.idiomatic: Forcibly drafting civilians was already forbidden by law.

sentences.zh: 所司莫能體上意，執民為兵。

translations.literal: The responsible offices could not grasp the court's intent and seized commoners as soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Local offices ignored the court's intent and simply seized people for the ranks.

sentences.zh: 或甘言誑誘，或詐名賈舟，候負販者群至，輒載之去；

translations.literal: Some used sweet words to deceive and lure; some falsely posed as merchants in boats, waited until porters and peddlers gathered in groups, then carried them off;
translations.idiomatic: Some lured men with smooth talk; others posed as traders, waited for porters to gather, and hauled them away;

sentences.zh: 或購航船人，全船疾趨所隸；

translations.literal: some bought off ferrymen and rushed whole boats to their jurisdiction;
translations.idiomatic: some bribed ferry crews to rush entire boats to their camps;

sentences.zh: 或令軍婦冶容誘於路，盡涅刺之。

translations.literal: some ordered soldiers' wives to dress alluringly and entice men on the roads, then tattooed them all.
translations.idiomatic: some sent soldiers' wives to dress up and bait travelers on the road, then tattoo every man they caught.

sentences.zh: 由是野無耕人，途無商旅，往往聚丁壯數十，而後敢入市。

translations.literal: Hence in the fields there were no plowmen, on the roads no merchants or travelers; often men had to gather several dozen stalwarts before daring enter the market.
translations.idiomatic: Fields stood empty of farmers and roads of merchants; men often marched into town only in bands of dozens for safety.

sentences.zh: 民有被執而赴水火者，有自斷指臂以求免者，有與軍人抗而殺傷者，無賴乘機假名為擾。

translations.literal: Some commoners seized threw themselves into fire or water; some cut off fingers or arms to seek release; some fought soldiers and wounded or killed them; ruffians seized the chance to harass under false pretenses.
translations.idiomatic: Some captives drowned or burned themselves; others maimed their hands to escape; some fought recruiters and killed them; and hoodlums used the chaos to prey on the public.

sentences.zh: 考之舊制，凡軍有闕額即招填。

translations.literal: Examining the old system, whenever an army had quota shortfalls it recruited to fill them.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rules, any unit short of quota was to recruit replacements.

sentences.zh: 熙寧、元豐講求民兵之政，於是募兵浸減，而三衙多虛籍。

translations.literal: In Xining and Yuanfeng the court pursued militia policy, whereupon recruited troops gradually diminished while the Three Bureaus held many fictitious rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Xining and Yuanfeng reforms stressed militia, so hired armies shrank while the Three Palace Bureaus kept bloated, hollow rolls.

sentences.zh: 至於靖康，禁衛弱矣。

translations.literal: By the time of Jingkang, the Forbidden Guard had grown weak.
translations.idiomatic: By Jingkang the Palace Guards had withered.

sentences.zh: 中興復用招募。

translations.literal: After the restoration, recruitment was used again.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration the court returned to recruitment.

sentences.zh: 立等杖，選勇壯，核人才，驗虛實，審刺之法雖在諸屯，而已招者兵籍悉總於樞府雲。

translations.literal: Height staffs were set, the brave and stalwart selected, talent verified, truth and falsehood checked; though tattoo review methods remained in the various garrisons, the rolls of those already recruited were all consolidated at the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Standards of height, courage, and fitness were restored and fraud was audited; although local camps still tattooed recruits, every enrolled man's record was held at the Bureau of Military Affairs.
